News.title: Teen pupils, 17, 14 & 13 die after being swept out to sea while playing as boy, 12, pulled from water in dramatic rescue
News.content:
SEA TRAGEDY Teen pupils, 17, 14 & 13 die after being swept out to sea while playing as boy, 12, pulled from water in dramatic rescue

THREE teenagers have drowned after a horrifying rescue attempt ended in tragedy when they were swept out to sea while playing on rocks.

Brothers Haruki Shitaebisu, 17, and Kensei, 13, and their friend Takahiro Takemoto, 14, were among four youngsters dragged into the deadly waters.

The horror unfolded off Ichikikushikino in Kagoshima Prefecture, southwestern Japan, at around 3.30pm on Friday.

Facing the open sea, the rocky coastline became the scene of a nightmare after four students started jumping into the water and two suddenly got into trouble.





Desperate to save them, the other two plunged in – only to be swept away themselves.

A fifth student who escaped the terrifying ordeal desperately called for help, while a 12-year-old boy was pulled to safety by a Coast Guard patrol vessel.

But the other three vanished beneath the waves, triggering a frantic search that continued into Saturday.

Two bodies were recovered from the sea on Saturday morning and the boys were confirmed dead.

A third was found later that afternoon in a state of cardiopulmonary arrest and was also confirmed dead.

The Coast Guard identified two of the dead as Haruki and Takemoto, while the identity of the third was still being investigated.

Haruki’s younger brother Kensei remains missing.

Rough waves had been predicted for the area, although no wave warning or advisory had been issued for the coastal area of Ichikikushikino City.



The Coast Guard initially said the area was off-limits for swimming, but later corrected the information and said swimming is allowed there.

Another report said swimming is prohibited at the site.

The desperate search continued on Saturday as winds and waves appeared calmer than the previous day.

It comes just after a Brit dad died after being swept away in a rip tide while swimming with his wife and three kids in Indonesia.

They were out swimming at Kerandangan Beach at around 3.30pm on Wednesday when the father was suddenly taken by a rip tide.



He was missing underwater for 18 minutes before being pulled unconscious from the waves.

Local residents had rushed to his aid with a jet ski and diving equipment.

The dad was rushed to hospital but could not be saved.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His wife and three children survived the ordeal.

They had been staying at the Rinjani Eco Resort in Tanjung, North Lombok, a holiday island near Bali.

News.title: Growing business can bag Burnham a triple bullseye – it’s time for PM to hit the target
News.content:
‘Deluded’ PM must listen to business

ANDY BURNHAM’S honeymoon is well and truly over.

On Tuesday he will finally have to stand up in Parliament and tell MPs what his plans really are.



The weeks of carefully placed soundbites and soft policy initiatives will finally be met with the hard reality of hostile questioning.

It is time for some straight talking, particularly on the economy.



Last week Mr Burnham was making sympathetic noises to the business community.

He has indicated that helping firms will be one of the big themes when he addresses MPs.



The PM said he was “acutely conscious” of how hard the trading environment is on the High Street and vowed: “I’m trying to make life easier.”

But it all sounds like classic Burnhamism.

Warm words to lift expectations tempered by the “challenging” fiscal backdrop.

His predecessor Sir Keir Starmer liked to call this “realistic hope”. And look where that got him.



If the PM really wants to help he must cut business taxes and lower the cost of creating jobs.

But don’t just take our word for it, Mr Burnham. Listen to the people who actually run big firms.

Mike Ashley employs 30,000 people. He calls the PM’s ideas on reviving the High Street “delusional”.

Lord Stuart Rose was boss of Marks and Spencer, which employs 65,000 people. He called Mr Burnham’s plans “a lot of b******s”.

And today Lord Richard Walker, chairman of the Iceland supermarket which employs almost 30,000, has a direct message: “Make it cheaper to employ people, invest and grow.”



If Mr Burnham wants to help employers he must listen to their critical voices.

Growing business not only boosts the economy, it also gets Neets into work and lowers the welfare bill.

That’s a triple bullseye.

Make sure you hit the target, PM.

We’ve hit a brick wall

RUINOUS energy costs don’t just wreck family budgets.



They also hold back our industry.

Construction experts say British-made bricks are now so expensive that it is cheaper to buy them from Europe.

Last year we imported a staggering 352million.

This crushing energy price burden is stifling firms and jobs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

As he plans his budget, Andy Burnham should remember one thing:



You can’t build a better Britain if it is all made from foreign bricks.

News.title: Moment driver, 34, leads cops on 130mph police chase while high on cocaine & cannabis before getting stuck in traffic
News.content:
THIS is the moment a female driver led cops on a 13-mile chase while high on a cocktail of cocaine and cannabis.

Tia Paget, 34, undertook cars at high speeds and cut off a vehicle on a roundabout before police were able to stop her.



Shocking video footage shows the black Vauxhall Insignia dodging through traffic on a major road in Hampshire.

The car was seen cutting off a lorry on a roundabout during the chaotic and dangerous drive.



The 34-year-old driver failed to stop for police and then triggered the chase back in April.

Paget tried to avoid cops by reaching speeds of up to 130mph.

Swerving across lanes and dodging through cars, Paget put other road users in danger as she drove under the influence.

Officers were eventually able to stop her as she got caught in traffic.



The crook then failed a cannabis and cocaine test at the roadside, along with small quantities of the drugs found in her car.

Paget appeared at Portsmouth Crown Court on August 20 and was sentenced for charges of drug driving, dangerous driving, driving without insurance, possession of cocaine, and possession of cannabis.

She was banned from driving for four years, and handed a sentence of 10 months imprisonment which was suspended for two years.

Paget was also ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and 12 rehabilitation requirement days.

News.title: Cops probe death of man, 41, killed by falling sign at Christian festival
News.content:
THE death of a man killed by a falling sign at a Christian festival is being investigated by police.

They are examining whether or not the structure was properly secured before it collapsed, with witnesses claiming it was blown over by strong winds.



The 41-year-old man, from Eastbourne, East Sussex, was crushed when a huge wooden archway gave way on Friday.

Another six people were injured, two seriously.



Fred Abbott, a father of four, was sitting nearby when the structure fell at the sell-out Big Church Festival near Steyning, West Sussex.

He described hearing a “massive crack and bang” and joined an estimated 30 to 50 people who scrambled to lift the heavy wooden sign off the injured festival-goers.



Archbishop of Canterbury Dame Sarah Mullally was said to be “sad and shocked” by the fatality.

She said: “I pray for his family, friends and loved ones as they grieve.

“I pray for those receiving treatment, and the healthcare workers looking after them.

“And I pray too for the other festival-goers, staff and event organisers as they come to terms with these tragic events.



“May the God of comfort and healing be with them all.”

The three-day event, founded in 2009, is the UK’s biggest Christian music festival with all 40,000 tickets sold.

Organisers later cancelled the event and said: “Big Church Festival is about bringing people together. That community is grieving. We are heartbroken.”



Det Chief Supt Richard McDonagh, of Sussex Police, said: “This is a tragic incident and our thoughts go out to the man’s family and friends at this incredibly difficult time.

“I recognise the immense distress this will have caused people at the festival, and we are working with a number of partners as we seek to establish exactly what happened.

“We’re urging anyone with information to come forward.”

News.title: Vessel carrying five people ‘in distress’ in the English Channel as coastguard launches major rescue mission
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SHIP ALERT Vessel carrying five people ‘in distress’ in the English Channel as coastguard launches major rescue mission

A VESSEL carrying five people is “in distress” in the English channel, sparking a major rescue mission.

More than 15 lifeboats have raced to reports of a boat in trouble off the coast of Plymouth at around 6pm.



A helicopter, an aircraft and several lifeboats have plunged into the channel to save the troubled vessel.

“HM Coastguard is co-ordinating the response to a report of a vessel in distress with five people on board, south west of Eddystone Lighthouse”, confirmed the Maritime and Coastguard Agency.



They added: “A coastguard rescue helicopter and a fixed wing aircraft have been sent, together with RNLI lifeboats from Falmouth and Plymouth. Local vessels are also assisting.

“The incident is ongoing and there is no further information at this time”.



Local paper PlymouthPlus reported that a French fishing vessel sunk off the Plymouth coast.

A French warship has also joined the hunt for survivors, according to the outlet.

Boats from both Plymouth and Falmouth have also been deployed.

Just after 9pm a coastguard helicopter from Newquay that had been scouring the seas for the boat returned to land to refuel. It is expected to rejoin the search party afterwards.

News.title: Piers Morgan chips in £1,000 to help cricket ace fly from his wedding to Lord’s by helicopter
News.content:
CRICKET fan Piers Morgan has chipped in £1,000 to help a bridegroom pay for a private helicopter so he can play at Lord’s the day after his wedding.

Team captain Peter Melhuish, 32, was delighted when his side Blackheath CC won a place in the Cawston Press Village Cup final.



But the match is to be held at the North West London ground the day after Peter marries 32-year-old Izzy Upton 240 miles away in Abergele, North Wales.

The five-hour road trip would mean a 5am taxi for next Sunday’s 11am start.



But a £10,000 flight would be about an hour.

Piers, also a village cricketer, said: “I’m glad you will now be living my dream. Good luck.”

Peter, from Guildford, Surrey, said: “It’d be amazing if we can pull something together.”

“The only other way is a 5am taxi down from the wedding which wouldn’t be much fun.

“It’s amazing how the club are pulling together and helping us with it.

“It’s really nice to have that support from them.



Peter said bride-to-be Izzy had been “great” despite the potential changes to their plans on September 6.

“We’ve been organising the wedding for well over a year so the fixtures for the Village Cup hadn’t even come out when we started organising it.

“She’s been really supportive and very understanding of how much it means, not just to me but the club too.”

News.title: Grieving parents demand answers after boss ‘ambushed’ daughter, 26, over office complaint that led her to take own life
News.content:
'VEXATIOUS' CLAIMS Grieving parents demand answers after boss ‘ambushed’ daughter, 26, over office complaint that led her to take own life

THE GRIEVING parents of a Treasury employee who took her own life have demanded answers after she was “ambushed” by bosses over an office complaint.

Chloe Moffat, 26, died on May 20 last year, a day after she was called into a disciplinary meeting and accused of sharing confidential information.



A coroner found earlier this month how the Treasury had “materially contributed” to Chloe’s death after the department failed to follow its own policies.

The personal assistant from Brixton, South London, had not been reassured by management that her job was safe – even though she was unlikely be sacked.



Chloe, who “loved her job” and had an “exemplary employment record”, was left in a state of “distress” following the meeting.

Her parents have now blasted the accusations against their daughter as “vexatious” and “nothing more than office gossip”, reports The Times.

On May 19, Chloe was given just five minutes’ notice before she was called into a meeting with two managers.

She was subsequently informed that two colleagues had alleged she had shared confidential information about other employees – claims Moffat denied.



Chloe’s mum, questioned why bosses didn’t examine if the claims were “credible, consistent with Chloe’s character and if they could perhaps have been malicious”.

“When her line manager heard them, she said they didn’t sound like the Chloe she knew,” she said.

“So why ambush her with a meeting like this without checking if they were vexatious, unfounded or simply not true?”

When Chloe asked whether she’d lose her job, the senior manager said she “could not predict the outcome at this stage”.

After the meeting, she temporarily lost access to her director’s email inbox and diary and advised not to speak to colleagues about the allegations and potential investigation.



Chloe’s father, David said: “After her death, when we were trying to work out how bad the complaints had been for a meeting like this to be called that led to Chloe taking the drastic action she did, we finally saw the allegations and thought, ‘Was that it?’”

He added that her colleagues said “it was nothing more than office gossip” and questioned why she hadn’t been “reassured this was the case”.

One friend said she received a text from her on the same day as the proceedings which read: “I am going to be fired.”

How to get help EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. The pair met up in central London where Chloe “broke down crying” and was “distressed” by the allegations.

Chloe also spoke to her mum who said the 26-year-old was convinced she wouldn’t be able to return to her role even if she kept her job “because she no longer knew who she could trust”.



After speaking to her father, Chloe had agreed to stay at the family’s home in Surrey where they talked about a potential weekend trip to Oxford.

But the next morning, David tragically discovered his daughter’s body – the coroner ruled her death as suicide.

Her father said that she had been left so distraught by what had happened that “in her eyes, her life was destroyed” and labelled it as “unforgivable”.

David added that he didn’t feel the Treasury had taken responsibility but permanent secretary James Bowler had agreed to meet the family in September.

Assistant coroner Anna Crawford previously told Surrey coroners’ court: “The evidence establishes a clear sequence of events.



“Had Chloe been properly supported and advised of her rights before the meeting, she would not have been so devastated and isolated.”

She said she would be sending a prevention of future deaths report to HM Treasury, the head of the civil service and to Acas.

A Treasury spokesperson said: “Our deepest sympathies continue to be with Chloe’s family, and the department continues to mourn Chloe’s death.

“We are taking all concerns extremely seriously and are considering the coroner’s findings carefully.

“We have introduced improvements to guidance, support and wellbeing arrangements but recognise we must continue to take action to prevent this happening again.”

News.title: Car wash firm fined for employing illegal staff still holds licence to sponsor foreign workers
News.content:
A CAR wash firm fined for employing illegal staff still holds a licence to sponsor foreign nationals on skilled worker visas.

Mayfair Carwash, which cleans motors for up to £50, was hit with the £160,000 penalty this year after a Home Office raid.



The Sun On Sunday visited the business this week and the man identified by staff as the manager shrugged when asked about the fine.

Marble Arch Express Ltd runs the car wash in central London and holds the Home Office licence on skilled worker visas.



The Home Office says our findings will form part of a probe into what businesses can bring in skilled work.

Currently, vape shops, kebab takeaways and car washes remain on the sponsorship list despite calls for unemployed British youngsters to be given more chances to work.



When The Sun on Sunday visited the business visited this week, we were led to a man identified by staff as the car wash’s manager.

The staff member did not comment and instead shrugged his shoulders when confronted about the six-figure fine.

Across an hour on Friday afternoon, two dozen cars were cleaned at the high-end firm, which is just around the corner from the capital’s most lucrative high street.

Owners of flashy Mercedes motors, BMWs, and Range Rovers had their vehicles jet-washed by hand for up to £50 a pop.



Over a dozen members of staff could be seen milling around the business’s premises throughout the afternoon.

Analysis of Home Office penalty records shows car washes were hit with fines totalling £2,595,000 for using illegal labour between January and March.

But some 39 car washes are licensed to sponsor non-British nationals.

News.title: British right-wing commentator Milo Yiannopoulos deported after calling for 'zero immigration'
News.content:
British right-wing commentator Milo Yiannopoulos deported after calling for 'zero immigration'

Milo Yiannopoulos, 'an illegal alien from the UK' had been sent back home after choosing to 'overstay his welcome,' the US Department of Homeland Security said

View 2 Images Milo Yiannopoulos was detained by ICE and deported back to the UK (Image: US Department of Homeland Security/AFP via Getty Images)

British right-wing provocateur Milo Yiannopoulos has been deported back to the UK after being detained by US immigration officials.

‌



The 41-year-old, who previously cheered on ICE raids, flew into the US in May 2019 and "chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation's laws", the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said.

‌



The former editor of Breitbart News and close associate to rapper Kanye West was referred to by immigration officials as an "illegal alien," reports the BBC.

‌



A DHS spokesperson said in a statement given to the broadcaster that Yiannopoulos, "an illegal alien from the United Kingdom" had been sent "back to his home country".

He was returned to the UK today after being arrested at the Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport in Louisiana on Thursday having failed to appear at an immigration hearing.

View 2 Images Immigration officials called Yiannopoulos an 'illegal alien' (Image: AP Photo/Julio Cortez)

‌



Yiannopoulos has previously labelled himself "the most fabulous supervillain on the internet" and has championed alt-right talking points on feminism, Islam and immigrants.

He has been especially supportive of US President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown. "Zero immigration for the next 20 years. No ifs, no buts," he wrote on X last year.

Immigration officials noted that Mr Yiannopoulos initially arrived legally in the US in 2019.

‌



"Yiannopoulos legally entered the country on May 14 2019, through New York City, New York. He chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation's laws," a spokesperson said.

"Yiannopoulos was issued a final order of removal by an immigration judge on July 22, after failing to show up for his immigration hearing. He will remain in Ice custody pending removal."

They added that being in detention was a "choice" as the US government is offering money and free flights for people to "self deport".

Article continues below

In the early 2010s, Mr Yiannopoulos was recruited to the Breitbart website by Mr Trump’s former chief strategist Steve Bannon, and was known to refer to Donald Trump as "daddy".

He resigned from the company in 2017 after a video of him endorsing paedophilia resurfaced online, and later apologised for the remarks and said he had been a victim of sexual assault as a minor.

He more recently ran a short-lived presidential campaign for the rapper Ye (formerly Kanye West) and reportedly worked as an intern for former Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene.

News.title: Fuming neighbours of 'mega mansion built without permission' want it torn down
News.content:
Fuming neighbours of 'mega mansion built without permission' want it torn down

The massive mansion on the edge of the historic city of Bath is facing calls to be torn down after some locals claimed it was proof how the wealthy were able to find loopholes in the planning process

View 5 Images Local residents are opposed to the new property (Image: Tom Wren / SWNS)

Neighbours of a "mega mansion" believed to be the biggest new-build home in Bath in 100 years are demanding it be torn down after it was built without planning permission.

‌



The massive mansion on the edge of the historic city has been built significantly higher than what was approved, according to the residents. Tavis Hamilton, 48, lives next door to the massive house and has spent 10 years battling developers.

‌



He is now one of more than 100 locals to object to the build, but locals fear the council has left it too late to carry out any meaningful enforcement. With the building now "topped out" and nearly complete, a retrospective application has now been submitted to "validate" the changes from the original plans.

‌



But some locals claim it highlighted how multi-millionaires were able to abuse and find loopholes during the the planning process. Bath and North-East Somerset Council declined to comment on the build and said enforcement action would only be "considered" after the fresh application has been determined.

View 5 Images Locals claim the mansion highlights how millionaires took advantage of the planning process (Image: Tom Wren / SWNS)

House designed by Isambard Kingdom Brunel goes on the market for £4m READ MORE :

But Tavis said: "It is an absolute mega home - it will prob be worth more than £3million when it's finished. It is enormous and dwarfs all the cottages. You could fit around 24 of the other cottages into the footprint.

‌



"It has been built for the last three years but it has now been topped out so you can see the full height and scale. It just shows how unfair the process is. It seems if you put the wrong guttering on your house or use the incorrect glazing, the council jump on you for enforcement.

"But you can build this enormous structure without the right planning permission and no enforcement is carried out until it is too late." More than 70 residents attended a recent site meeting and over 100 have lodged formal objections to the now seven-bedroom home, expressing their anger at the situation while building work continued.

Tavis, who lives there with his partner Charlotte Bolton and his daughter, said permission was initially granted for a low-lying single-storey building built into the hillside. But when the builders hit ground water they backfilled the hole with concrete, he claimed.

‌



The end result has been a home, he describes as, "significantly higher" than planned and in a different spot. It has gone through three different owners since 2007 and multiple planning applications - each time looking to increase its height and prominence, locals revealed.

View 5 Images Local residents said the orientation and height differ from the original plan (Image: Tom Wren / SWNS)

Enforcement teams have carried out a survey and confirmed several deviations from the approved plans - including the building being higher, larger and not in the approved spot.

‌



Tavis added: "The new application has been submitted as part of a wider game to avoid enforcement action. The changes are so significant and widespread that all the rest of the drawings from roof light location also require total update.

"A cease order needs to be applied to all works on site whilst a detailed new planning application is submitted. If this had been put in place when the concern over levels was first reported two years ago, when the concrete pad was poured, this could have been resolved then, reducing the damage that will now be more difficult and costly to rectify."

Local residents said the orientation, siting, height, volume, footprint and surrounding landscaping all "significantly" deviate from the original plans and would set a damaging precedent in the area.

‌



Tavis, who has lived there for 20 years, said the lane is full of very traditional Bath stone Georgian properties. He said landscaping and planting had also not been done as it should but the main source of anger was its increase in height and massing and increasing it from five bedrooms to seven.

View 5 Images The development "just changes to whatever" the owners want, a local councillor said (Image: Tom Wren / SWNS)

The plot was originally sold for £1million with planning and locals believe another million must have been spent on excavation. Another "monster mansion" has also been built the other side, and Tavis said his family were now "sandwiched between two of the largest single residences built in Bath in about 100 years".

‌



Locals said the original developer won permission for the biggest they could do on the plot despite a number of opposition and then put it straight on the market. It was then bought by a wealthy individual who went through the process of three or four more applications to make it higher and more prominent.

Among those objecting on the council website, another local added: "It was already noted as the largest house ever approved by the council, and now apparently will include seven bedrooms.

Local ward district councillor Joanna Wright said she backed the residents wanting enforcement action. She said: "It is outrageous. They got planning permission in 2013 and they haven't built it to that plan. They keep extending it and changing who owns it.

‌



"The development just changes to whatever they want to do. Enforcement was involved and asked them to stop. They said they would stop but then put in a variation on the plans and on it goes.

View 5 Images Locals said the original developer won permission for the biggest they could do on the plot despite opposition (Image: Tom Wren / SWNS)

"I've wrote again to enforcement and planning but why hasn't been dealt with by now I don' t know."

Article continues below

The applicant and house owner Thomas Worrall, of Yate near Bristol, said: "The whole street has been against me from day one. I only bought the site to build my own house with planning permission already on it. Someone else took it all to planning seven years ago.

"There have been complications on the ground and the professional builders were not able to make it work so it was a little bit higher to start with. The neighbours all seem to think I have screwed the system and been sneaky. But I am not. I've now pulled all my guys off site and trying to deal with the planners.

"It was just a few mistakes on site. They think I have all this money and want to play the system but that is 100 per cent not true. I just want an easy life. I want to get my house finished and move my family into it. Everything has now completely stopped on site."

News.title: Boy, 13, stabbed at Taco Bell in Rochdale as police swarm town centre
News.content:
Boy, 13, stabbed at Taco Bell in Rochdale as police swarm town centre

Two boys have been arrested after a 13-year-old boy was stabbed at a Taco Bell in Rochdale town centre and rushed to hospital with serious injuries, police said

View Image Police at the scene in Rochdale town centre (Image: ASP)

A 13-year-old boy has been rushed to hospital with serious injuries after being stabbed at a Taco Bell in Rochdale town centre.

An air ambulance and several police vehicles were scrambled to the scene shortly after 6pm, with officers placing a cordon around the fast-food chain.

Eyewitnesses inside Taco Bell had reported a "stabbing" before CSI officers arrived at the scene to conduct their enquiries.

‌



Two boys have been arrested on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article, Greater Manchester Police have said.

A spokesperson for the force said: "We were called to reports of a stabbing at 6.09pm on Riverside Walk. Boy, 13, taken to hospital with serious injuries.

"Two teenage boys have been arrested on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article. Enquiries are ongoing."

News.title: Burscough train crash - updates: One dead after train hits van near Liverpool
News.content:
Paramedics and fire crews surrounded a Northern train in West Lancashire after it collided with a van at a level crossing, leaving one dead and two injured

A man has died and two others have been injured after a train struck a van at a railway crossing in West Lancashire.

The Northern train had come to halt next to farmland in the Burscough area, with multiple ambulances and a fire engine dispatched to the scene.

One passenger posted an image of a damaged carriage with debris strewn across the floor. The passenger said they were still on the train with their children, adding "we are all shook".

The incident appears to have unfolded near Martin Lane in Burscough, near its junction with Whitehouse Lane, reports the Liverpool Echo.

Northern has blocked all lines between Wigan Wallgate and Southport "due to emergency services dealing with an incident," with disruption expected for the rest of the day.

The company said: "Northern train ticket restrictions have been lifted in the affected areas, including Advance and Peak restrictions, during this disruption. Restrictions will be reinstated once the disruption ends."

News.title: Amsterdam horror stabbing as three people knifed outside major train station
News.content:
Amsterdam horror stabbing as three people knifed outside major train station

A fourth person was taken to hospital and subsequently arrested following an incident outside Amsterdam Centraal Station

View Image Three people were stabbed just outside Amsterdam Central Station (Image: ANP/Shutterstock)

Three people have been stabbed outside a major train station in Amsterdam. Authorities confirmed a fourth person was also injured and arrested in an incident outside Amsterdam Centraal Station at around 7.30pm local time on Saturday, August 29.

It came after emergency services rushed the De Ruijterkade, at the rear of the major transport hub. According to Dutch news agency ANP, the three people were taken to hospital, although their condition is currently unknown.

A fourth person, believed to be the suspect, was also taken to hospital where they were subsequently arrested, ANP reports. The stabbing is understood to have happened at the station exit on the JJ side of Amsterdam Centraal.

Dutch public broadcaster NOS also reported that four people - the three victims and suspect - were taken to hospital. A major emergency response was triggered following the reported violence.

Four ambulances, a Mobile Medical Team and a specialist fire service team attended the scene, reports 112 Nieuws Nederland. Images from the scene published by Dutch-based AD show firefighters wearing bulletproof vests as they attended the scene.

Article continues below

And a police spokesman told 112 Nieuws Nederland that the incident followed a fight. De Ruijterkade was closed while emergency services investigated the scene, with AD also reporting part of the station itself was cordoned off while forensic investigators worked in the area.

Police have appealed for anyone who might have seen the incident or has any information to come forward. No information has yet been released about the severity of the injuries, according to 112 Nieuws Nederland. The investigation remains ongoing.

News.title: Life expectancy revealed as men in 10 UK areas have fewer than 50 years of good health - check yours
News.content:
Life expectancy revealed as men in 10 UK areas have fewer than 50 years of good health - check yours

Men statistically live shorter lives than women in Britain, with the average man living 79.4 years while women live an average of 83.3 years, according to the Office for National Statistics

View 3 Images Blackpool was had one of the lowest healthy life expectancy rates (Image: Getty Images)

Male life expectancy in England and Wales has been revealed with 10 areas showing where men will have fewer than 50 years of good health - check your area below.

‌



Figures from the Office for National Statistics revealed the average healthy life expectancy in every neighbourhood in England and Wales. The figures are based on an estimate of years spent in "very good" or "good" general health, based on how individuals perceive their general health.

‌



Staggering statistics revealed all by two of the 10 areas where men will have less than 50 years of good health were in the North. The North is also home to half of the 1,400 neighbourhoods where healthy life expectancy is less than 60 years of age.

‌



View 3 Images Lincolnshire is one of the regions with the lowest healthy life expectancy (Image: Geography Photos/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

UK town named the healthiest with the longest life expectancy in the country READ MORE :

Our new map reveals how long people born in your local area can expect to live in good health. It reveals the huge gaps within cities across the nation, but also how there are many areas below the national average in healthy life expectancy.

Where is lowest health life expectancy in country?

‌



The Central Stockton & Portrack area of Stockton-on-Tees has the lowest healthy life expectancy in the country. Men born in the area can expect just 47.7 years of good health.

In Birkenhead Central in Wirral, the average is just 47.8 years, in Central Blackpool it's 47.9 years and in Grimsby Easy Marsh & Port in North East Lincolnshire it's 48.0. That region in North East Lincolnshire is also the only place in the country where women have a healthy life expectancy of less than 50 years, with just 49.0 years of healthy life.

People living in the Knightsbridge, Belgravia & Hyde Park area of London can expect to enjoy a longer healthy life than those anywhere else in England and Wales. The average healthy life expectancy for men in the area is 78.3 years and 81.2 years for women. Those are the longest healthy life expectancies of any small area, according to the latest figures from the Office for National Statistics.

‌



A report by the Joseph Rowntree Foundation (JRF) found that poverty is the biggest driver in the gaps in healthy life expectancy. The report found a woman living in the least deprived areas of the country will spend 82 per cent of their life in good health.

View 3 Images Knightsbridge is one of the areas with one of the highest life expectancies (Image: James Willoughby/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

That drops to just 65 per cent in the most deprived areas, equating to 20 fewer years of life in good health. For males the gap is 19 years, with men in the least deprived areas spending 85 per cent of their lives in good health compared to 70 per cent in the most deprived areas.

Article continues below

Scot Hunter, Analyst at the Joseph Rowntree Foundation, says: "It isn’t right that where you live impacts how long you can expect to live in good health. It’s striking but not surprising that people who spend more of their life in poor health are more likely to live in places that lost key industries: like manufacturing and mining towns as well as seaside towns and inner-city neighbourhoods.

"We know that as well as struggling economically, many of these areas have lost the community groups, places and activities that brought people together. Compared to similar places that still have their community centres, youth clubs and sports halls, people in these doubly disadvantaged areas are more likely to be living in poor health.

"The story isn’t just about the economies of these places, but whether there’s someone or somewhere in your neighbourhood that helps you feel connected, confident and in control. We need to invest in this vital infrastructure if we want people in every place to live healthier, more resilient lives."

News.title: Coastguard helicopter scrambled as boat 'in distress' English Channel off Plymouth
News.content:
Coastguard helicopter scrambled as boat 'in distress' English Channel off Plymouth

A boat with five people onboard as reported

View Image The coastguard rescue helicopter has been dispatched alongside lifeboats (Image: Getty Images)

A vessel with five people on board is “in distress” in the English Channel, the coastguard has said.

‌



A rescue has been launched to try to help the vessel which is in trouble south west of Eddystone Lighthouse and off Plymouth, the Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) said.

‌



It was alerted by a report about the vessel just after 6pm on Saturday. A rescue helicopter, a fixed wing aircraft and RNLI lifeboats are among the vessels which have been scrambled to the scene.

‌



No further details are currently available about the vessel or the nature of the incident.

In a statement, the MCA said: “HM Coastguard is co-ordinating the response to a report of a vessel in distress with five people on board, south west of Eddystone Lighthouse.”

Article continues below

It added: “A coastguard rescue helicopter and a fixed wing aircraft have been sent, together with RNLI lifeboats from Falmouth and Plymouth. Local vessels are also assisting.

“The incident is ongoing and there is no further information at this time.”

News.title: MPs set to agree £100million grant to King Charles as critics blast 'royal rip off'
News.content:
MPs set to agree £100million grant to King Charles as critics blast 'royal rip off'

The government's Sovereign Grant Bill will see the sum given to the royal family slashed by £40million a year, but critics argue it is almost double the amount it should be

View 4 Images The Sovereign Grant is set to total just under £100million next year

Andy Burnham is under pressure to go further in slashing the amount of taxpayer cash given to the royal family - with MPs set to approve a £100million annual grant.

‌



On Tuesday the Treasury will put forward legislation cutting the Sovereign Grant by nearly £40million. But King Charles will still be given £99.9million to carry out his duties and maintain royal palaces - a sum critics say is excessive.

‌



The amount given to the royals has rocketed in the past 15 years despite the number of working royals falling. Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was stripped of his titles amid the toxic fallout over his friendship with paedophile Jeffrey Epstein.

‌



And Prince Harry and Meghan quit the Firm in 2020 and moved to the US, only to make a shock return to Britain last week raising fears the taxpayer may end up forking out for the couple’s security.

Former Lib Dem minister Norman Baker, a firm critic of the monarchy, told The Mirror that the PM must "stop this royal rip-off now".

‌



View 4 Images The grant soared to pay for refurbishment of Buckingham Palace (Image: VV Shots via Getty Images)

The grant is an annual payment to fund the monarch's official duties, such as overseas trips. In April King Charles was praised for his handling of Donald Trump during a state visit to the US.

The payment - based on profits from the Crown Estate - also covers the cost of palace maintenance and employing staff. But critics say the proposed 2027/28 grant is more than double what it should be.

‌



The sum is more than three times the initial £31million allocated by Chancellor George Osborne when the Sovereign Grant was introduced in 2012/13. It had soared by more than £100million to £137.9million this year, largely due to a decade-long refurbishment at Buckingham Palace costing £369million.

New legislation needs to be passed in order to reduce the grant. In a briefing note sent to Labour MPs, anti-monarchy campaign group Labour for a Republic said: "The grant for 2027-28 should not, in real terms, be more that the Grant’s starting point in 2012-13: that would mean a Grant around £45m.

"The Royal Family is smaller that it was in 2011 and the King and Prince of Wales claim to favour a slimmed-down monarchy. Making the anticipated increase to £99.9m, when the Government cannot afford many of the changes it wants to make to tackle poverty and deprivation, would be wrong and would appear to be wrong."

‌



View 4 Images Former Lib Dem minister Norman Baker hit out at the 'royal rip off' (Image: In Pictures via Getty Images)

The group called for a complete overhaul of the way the royals are funded, breaking the link between Crown Estate profits and the sum handed over. It also urged the government to take the King's income - which it estimates at around £20million a year - from the Duchy of Lancaster into account.

Labour for a Republic secretary Ken Richie said: "Whatever one’s views on the monarchy, questions must be asked about why it needs so much more money now than it did in 2012."

‌



In the year to March 31, the royal annual financial report showed £5.1million was spent on travel, £33.7million on payroll and £3.5million on housekeeping and hospitality. Property maintenance totalled £67.5million.

Nearly £127,000 was spent on travel for the King and Queen to make an official visit to Rome last April. And documents show £733,000 was spent on 177 helicopter flights over 12 months. And 60 charter flights cost £837,000 in that time.

The government said it has no intention of ripping up the Sovereign Grant system. Earlier this year Labour grandee Baroness Margaret Hodge - who was appointed anti-corruption tsar in 2024 - said: "It's (the Sovereign Grant) run out of time."

‌



View 4 Images Baroness Margaret Hodge has previously called for an overhaul of royal funding (Image: PA)

She also called for more transparency around the royals' private wealth. The King has an estimated net worth of £680million, according to the Sunday Times Rich List, while accounts for the Sovereign Grant this year showed for the first time that Prince William is richer than his father, with a net worth of £1.2billion via the Duchy of Cornwall.

A Sunday Mirror investigation in 2024 found the Duchy of Cornwall made an average of £3.3million a year from selling properties from 2010 to 2020.

‌



But in the four years after this, this soared to £11million a year - but it is exempt from capital gains tax. Critics have argued the two Duchies should be public assets, but successive Governments have accepted them as private wealth.

Buckingham Palace said the King has voluntarily paid more than £30million in tax since ascending to the throne. In a statement in June, James Chalmers, Keeper of The Privy Purse, said: "It is important to emphasise that the Sovereign Grant does not provide personal income to members of the Royal Family. It funds the work of the institution – not private lives or private wealth."

And he continued: "This is not a blank cheque. Expenditure is governed by the same standards and disciplines as any publicly funded body, with strict value-for-money requirements, detailed planning, multi-year strategies, independent audit, and Treasury oversight."

‌



The Sovereign Grant is a sum set each year by the Royal Trustees - comprising the Prime Minister, the Chancellor, and the Keeper of the Privy Purse.

Under a deal reached during the coalition Government, the grant is calculated based on the profit of the Crown Estate. In the past decade, over £5billion of profits from the Crown Estate have been paid to the Exchequer.

A Treasury spokesman told The Mirror: "The Grant - which funds official business and doesn't provide an income to any members of the Royal Family – will fall by over 25% next year as the temporary funding for the reservicing of Buckingham Palace ends.

Article continues below

"The settlement is evidence‑based and reflects an increase in core activities like state visits and overseas trips. This supports government objectives and the UK's position on the world stage."

News.title: Cleverly quits shadow cabinet to run for London mayor
News.content:
Conservative MP Sir James Cleverly has said he is resigning from the shadow cabinet to run for London mayor.

"I am putting myself forward to be the Conservative candidate for mayor of London, because our capital needs more than an administrator," he wrote in the Times, external.

Sir James said he has told Tory leader Kemi Badenoch he is stepping down as shadow housing secretary, saying: "I must be free to speak about every aspect of London's future and concentrate fully on winning this race."

The capital is not set to vote on a new mayor until May 2028. Labour incumbent Sir Sadiq Khan is yet to confirm whether he will seek an unprecedented fourth term.

The Conservatives are yet to pick their candidate for the London mayoral race.

A source close to Badenoch said Cleverly "is a formidable politician and will out-campaign Khan".

Sir James, who was foreign secretary under former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, wrote that he intended to make London a city to be proud of again.

"We must rebuild its reputation and make it, once again, the best place in the world to live, work, invest and build a business," he added.

A senior Conservative politician, Sir James has held a number of ministerial positions under three prime ministers - including roles as home secretary and education secretary.

The army reservist represented the Tories on the London Assembly before his election as MP for Braintree in 2015.

After rising through the backbenches, he unsuccessfully ran for Conservative party leader in 2024, losing out to Badenoch.

Reacting to Sir James's announcement, a source said Badenoch "really didn't want James to leave shadow cabinet", but believed "he will be a big asset in London".

Current London Mayor Sir Sadiq began his first term in 2016. Cleverly wrote that the capital has been "let down by Labour".

He accused Prime Minister Andy Burnham of treating London as a "cash cow: somewhere to tax, regulate, raid and blame".

Sir James said: "Londoners need homes they can afford to buy or rent. Entrepreneurs need to be able to start and grow businesses without being strangled by cost and regulation."

The last time Londoners voted for their mayor in May 2024, Sir Sadiq beat Conservative rival Susan Hall by more than 275,000 votes - representing a swing of 3.2% to Labour.

The mayor won nine of the 14 constituencies including two gains from the Tories, and gained 43.8% of the vote share.

Reform UK revealed its candidate for the May 2028 election in January when it announced Westminster City councillor Laila Cunningham would be standing.

Reacting on social media, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage wrote the Conservatives are "done for", and said Cleverly "will not be the first Tory MP to give up any hope of winning their seat in Essex".

Cleverly has not resigned as an MP yet.

His announcement follows speculation in recent weeks that he would step down and launch a bid to become London's next mayor.

During his time at the London Assembly, Cleverly chaired the London Fire and Emergency Planning Authority, and also worked for Boris Johnson while he was mayor of London.

News.title: Sarah Ferguson expected back in the UK 'shortly', source says
News.content:
Ferguson is expected to move into the six-bedroom home "imminently", which could be as soon as next week, the Sun reported, external.

It is believed she has been spending her time out of the public eye at an Alpine chalet in Verbier, Switzerland, since leaving Royal Lodge. Her belongings were collected from Mountbatten-Windsor's home in Sandringham this week, the newspaper added.

She had been keeping a low profile since losing her titles alongside Mountbatten-Windsor after she became mired in the scandal about her connections to Epstein, and faced calls to speak to US authorities after last year's release of millions of documents shed new light on their relationship.

In one email exchange from 2011, she appeared to privately apologise for her public rejection of Epstein, saying: "You have always been a steadfast, generous and supreme friend to me and my family."

A spokesperson for the duchess previously said the email was sent after Epstein had threatened to sue her for defamation - in an effort to convince him not to.

Another email suggested Ferguson took her daughters to see Epstein in the US days after he was released from prison for child sex crimes.

The emails do not indicate any wrongdoing.

Epstein was also ultimately the downfall of Mountbatten-Windsor, who was stripped of his titles by the King because of "serious lapses of judgment" over his friendship with the late paedophile. Mountbatten-Windsor has always denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein.

Ferguson lost her courtesy royal divorcee title and reverted to her maiden name, and also lost the freedom of the city of York after councillors voted unanimously to remove the honour over the scandal.

Her expected return comes just days after the Duke and Duchess of Sussex came back to Britain with their children to begin a new life after six years living in the US.

News.title: Vessel in distress with five people onboard in Channel
News.content:
A vessel with five people on board is "in distress" in the English Channel, the coastguard has said.

A search and rescue helicopter and boats have been launched to try to help the vessel south west of Eddystone Lighthouse off Plymouth, the Maritime and Coastguard Agency said.

It said it was alerted just after 18:00 BST and a coastguard rescue helicopter and a fixed wing aircraft have been sent, together with RNLI lifeboats from Falmouth and Plymouth.

No further details are currently available about the vessel or the nature of the emergency.

News.title: 97-year-old woman rescued after Nepali floods looked like 'a warrior'
News.content:
A 97-year-old woman pulled from flood debris in Nepal is recovering in hospital, according to her doctors.

Guna Maya Bohara's great-nephew, Dipak Bohara, has told BBC Nepali she looked like "a warrior" who had returned victorious from battle.

The operation to pull Bohara out of the rubble of her care home took four hours.

Bohara travelled from Kathmandu to help rescue his great-aunt.

Hundreds of people have been confirmed dead after Wednesday's flash floods, which scientists believe were triggered by a glacier collapsing in the Himalayan border region with Tibet.

Video produced by Mansi Kapur and Kamal Pariyar. Video edited by Suneth Perera, Jasmin Dyer and Andrew Webb.

More on this story here.

News.title: Satellite images reveal scale of flood devastation in Nepal villages
News.content:
New satellite imagery has revealed the scale of the devastation along Nepal's Trishuli River caused by Wednesday's deadly flash flood, triggered by a glacier collapse.

Before-and-after images show how sections of the valley, where a torrent of floodwater and debris surged through, destroyed villages, bridges and hydroelectric power stations.

Hundreds of people have been killed and thousands more are missing, Nepalese officials say.

Among the worst-hit locations reviewed by BBC Verify was a key Nepal-Tibet border crossing, which was engulfed by a rush of floodwater and captured on camera.

The satellite imagery from US-based intelligence firm Vantor, shows the site has been almost entirely washed away. Shocking CCTV footage showed the moment as the deluge of water swept over buildings as people tried to escape.

News.title: What we know about the 33 British nationals missing in Nepal
News.content:
Families are flying out to Nepal to help the ongoing search for 33 British nationals still missing after deadly floods hit the country.

The brother of Neetu Goyal Tiwari, one of the missing Brits who has not been seen since Wednesday, has appealed to officials to locate his sister.

"Please help us find her", Naresh Goyal told the BBC as he struggled to hold back his emotions.

On Friday, Nepalese authorities named 573 tourists who are still missing in the country and despite fears of a second wave of flooding, search efforts have continued.

To help, the UK is deploying a rapid deployment team to Nepal to support British nationals affected in the region.

The specially-trained crisis response team is expected to arrive in Kathmandu on Saturday, a move that follows Prime Minister Andy Burnham's pledge of Â£5m worth of humanitarian support for relief and recovery efforts.

And as rescue efforts continue in the aftermath of the disaster which killed at least 538 people, details of the missing are slowly emerging.

News.title: We're behind UK's emergency phone alerts - but question how they're being used
News.content:
The government's Cobra emergency committee met to discuss how to respond. After sign off from Prime Minister Andy Burnham's de facto deputy Louise Haigh, the alert was sent at 19:00 on 14 August.

It triggered a backlash on social media with some vowing to opt out of further alerts in their phone settings, domestic abuse charities and survivors saying victims with hidden phones were put at risk, and confusion about alerts sent multiple times.

Dowden's worry is that the wildfire alert was more like a public information campaign than an imminent threat to life across all of England and Wales.

"People need to know that when they receive an alert, it is a genuine imminent emergency," the Conservative MP says. "If that confidence is lost, people will simply ignore it."

A Cabinet Office report during trials in 2014 warned of this "cry wolf" effect, while pointing out there was strong support among the public for the alerts.

"Alerts should not be issued just because the government wants to be seen to be doing something," Dowden adds.

The National Fire Chiefs Council said the alert heightened people's awareness and public behaviour, while government insiders point out wildfire alerts are commonplace in many European countries.

"By following the guidance that was issued, people were able to take the necessary steps to keep themselves safe and front line services recorded a significant decrease in incidents in the following days," a government spokesperson said.

But Frazer Rhodes, who worked in government across a decade to help build the technology and devise high thresholds for the alerts, feels a review is now necessary to avoid future ones backfiring.

He was in a bar in Halifax, West Yorkshire, with his wife when the sound of pinging phones began echoing around.

"Everybody around was just going, 'what's this?' What's this?'" he tells us. "Then my wife shouted, 'he did that'."

His wife's joke aside, he said his "immediate thought" was whether it met the threshold for sending one. He explains: "At its heart are three criteria: urgency, severity and certainty. So, in simple terms, how bad, how soon, and how sure?"

Rhodes thinks the wildfire alert arguably met the bar for urgency and severity, but perhaps not for certainty of a threat to life.

"It should be very rare to get an alert," he points out.

News.title: Burnham's summer tour is over - now he has to prove himself in Parliament
News.content:
Andy Burnham is set to come under the most intense scrutiny of his political life when Parliament returns on Tuesday.

Since coming to power six weeks ago, the new prime minister has largely been free to set his own agenda.

The timing of Labour's leadership contest meant he walked into Number 10 after the House of Commons began its summer break, denying MPs the chance to question him and creating what some have seen as a honeymoon period.

Burnham has embarked on what Downing Street called a "summer tour" of the UK, appeared on podcasts and announced a series of eye-catching policies, mainly aimed at tackling the cost of living.

But things are about to get a lot tougher, with MPs finally getting a chance to grill the new PM when he makes a statement to Parliament on his priorities as PM.

He has taken questions from MPs in the Commons before, when he was a minister in Tony Blair and Gordon Brown's Labour governments.

But Tuesday will be his first appearance on the government front bench for 16 years.

News.title: Christian festival 'devastated' after man's death
News.content:
Organisers of a Christian festival say they are "devastated" after a man died and six other people were injured by a falling sign.

Sussex Police said it had been called to the Big Church Festival at Wiston Park, near Steyning in West Sussex, at about 15:38 BST on Friday.

It was later confirmed a 41-year-old man from Eastbourne in East Sussex had died.

The Archbishop of Canterbury said she was "sad and shocked" to hear about the fatal incident.

Dame Sarah Mullally said: "I pray for his family, friends and loved ones as they grieve. I pray for those receiving treatment, and the healthcare workers looking after them.

"And I pray too for the other festival goers, staff and event organisers as they come to terms with these tragic events.

"May the God of comfort and healing be with them all."

South East Coast Ambulance service said four of the six people injured were taken to local hospitals for further treatment, with two people having serious injuries.

The Big Church Festival, which describes itself as the UK's biggest Christian festival, was founded in 2009.

The festival began on Friday and was due to continue until Sunday, but a decision was made by organisers to cancel the remainder of the event after the incident.

"We are working with the emergency services, police and the Health and Safety Executive as they establish the circumstances surrounding today's incident," the organisers said.

"We are incredibly grateful to everyone who responded, and to our teams and community for the care they have shown one another."

News.title: Football fans pay tribute to crash death officers
News.content:
Football fans and players have paid tribute to two Cleveland Police officers who were killed in a crash on Teesside.

PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough died in a head-on collision between their police car and a vehicle going the wrong way on the A66 near Middlesbrough early on 22 August. Five people in the other vehicle also died.

There was a minute's applause in their memory ahead of Middlesbrough and West Bromwich Albion's Championship match at Riverside Stadium, as pictures of the two men were displayed on a screen.

People also gathered to pay tribute at Seaton Carew FC's game against FC Hartlepool. PC Matthew Blades had been a junior football coach at both teams.

Seaton Carew FC coach Marcus Newing, who was friends with him, said the past week had been "horrendous", but seeing the "outpouring" from the nation had been "comforting".

"People would probably say that he's the goal of a dad and a husband," Newing said.

News.title: Strong winds and thunderstorms kick off the bank holiday weekend
News.content:
After weeks of scorching heat and drought the summer's swan song is set to be one of frequent downpours as well as gales for some.

Areas of heavy rain and showers are expected to sweep across parts of the UK on each day of the weekend, which is a bank holiday for many.

This could make for some soggy moments at many of the festivals taking place over the coming days.

Strong winds and gales may also cause problems for travellers and holidaymakers in southern parts of the UK.

News.title: Royal Navy warships track Russian vessels for three days in UK waters
News.content:
Royal Navy warships and a helicopter spent three days tracking Russian Navy vessels and sanctioned cargo ships in an "intense" operation in the North Sea and English Channel.

HMS Duncan, HMS St Albans and HMS Severn used radars to monitor four vessels last week, while a Merlin helicopter provided surveillance from the sky.

"Since that successful operation, we have seen Russian shadow fleet vessels increasingly forced to change their routes, imposing significant cost and delays to their journeys," Gen Sir Gwyn Jenkins, the First Sea Lord and Chief of Naval Staff, said.

It comes as data shows Royal Navy activity to monitor Russian movements is up 25% so far this year compared to 2025.

During the August operation, the Royal Navy warships including a Type 45 destroyer and a Type 23 frigate, tracked Russian destroyer Admiral Levchenko as it escorted sanctioned cargo vessels General Skobelev and Sparta south through the North Sea and into the English Channel.

The Royal Navy said Russia was "forced" to respond with "costly military resources" including the frigate Neustrashimy.

A statement said a Nato ally then took over monitoring off the coast of France, without specifying the country.

The operation comes after Royal Marine Commandos boarded a Russian "shadow fleet" oil tanker in the English Channel in June.

Marines joined by National Crime Agency (NCA) officers, with the support of the RAF, intercepted and boarded the Smyrtos in a six-hour operation - the first of its kind by UK armed forces.

NCA officers arrested an Indian national, 38, on suspicion of sanctions offences under the Russia Regulations and he was taken into custody.

News.title: Mother backs calls to stop killers' early release
News.content:
More than 30 families have called on the government to stop killers convicted of any form of manslaughter being released early to ease prison overcrowding in England and Wales.

In a letter to Justice Secretary Alex Norris, the families said they felt victims were "being asked to bear the consequences of the prison capacity crisis".

Signatories include Emma Webber, whose son Barnaby was stabbed to death in the Nottingham attacks in 2023, and whose killer Valdo Calocane was convicted of manslaughter on the basis of diminished responsibility.

Speaking on Radio 4's Today programme, Bridget Phillipson, Minister for Women and Equalities, defended the early release scheme.

She said the government had faced "some really difficult and unpalatable choices" in dealing with prison overcrowding and that they had faced "the wholesale collapse of the criminal justice system".

The scheme, external aims to ease prison overcrowding in England and Wales.

The families of those affected by homicide have called for those convicted of any form of manslaughter to be excluded.

Those convicted of murder and those serving sentences for rape, serious child sexual abuse and grooming offences are already excluded from the early release scheme.

News.title: Murder investigation after man found dead and child seriously injured
News.content:
A murder investigation has been launched after a man was found dead alongside a seriously injured child in County Tyrone on Saturday morning.

A male has been arrested on suspicion of murder and attempted murder and remains in custody.

The incident took place in Lisnahull Road in Dungannon.

The child was taken to the Royal Belfast Hospital for Sick Children.

Police are currently at the scene and have said the public should avoid the area while enquiries continue.

The Northern Ireland Ambulance Service (NIAS) said they received a 999 call at 11:08 BST on Saturday, following reports of an incident.

They dispatched a helicopter crew, three emergency crews, one advanced care paramedic, two ambulance officers and one HART (Hazardous Area Response Team) crew to the scene.

News.title: Woman detained in Egypt over 'sister's activism'
News.content:
A mother-of-four from Birmingham has been detained by the Egyptian authorities, with her husband and lawyer claiming it is due to her sister's online activism.

Eman el-Shazly, 45, from Handsworth Wood, was taken from her mother's house in Cairo in the early hours of Monday 17 August. Her husband, Zeesharn Moustapha, said this was 24 hours after Egyptian security forces "ram-raided" the property and told her: "You need to tell your sister to stop".

Three of el-Shazly's other siblings have also been detained, with her two brothers already being held when she was taken, and one of her sisters detained soon after.

The BBC has contacted the Egyptian consulate in London but has not had a response.

Moustapha said: "The family's a bit traumatised. [The children] are heartbroken.

"We really need the UK government to get their fingers out as quickly as possible."

A spokesperson for the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) said: "We are supporting the family of a British national detained in Egypt, and are in contact with the authorities."

News.title: Attempted murder arrest after man falls from balcony
News.content:
A man has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after a man fell from a balcony.

Police were called to reports that the man had fallen at flats on Liverpool Street in Salford shortly after midnight on Saturday, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said.

Emergency services attended and the man was taken to hospital with life-threatening injuries, where he remains in a critical condition, the force said.

A man in his 20s has been taken into police custody for questioning.

The incident has been referred to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) because the men had earlier contact with police, GMP said.

A blue forensic tent has been erected near to a building on the corner of Liverpool Street and Southern Street.

A local resident, who did not wish to be named, said she heard sirens overnight and saw the aftermath of the incident being live-streamed on social media.

She said: "I heard all the sirens, but I keep myself to myself so I didn't go out.

"I've seen it's all cordoned off and there's a blue forensics tent.

"It's sad, it's really sad. It's a bit close to home."

Ch Insp Lee Gridley said: "A man has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder, and he is currently being questioned in custody.

"Our officers are working at pace to establish the full circumstances, and a scene will remain in place whilst the investigation continues.

"We understand that incidents of this nature may cause concern within the community, however we believe this is an isolated incident and that there is no wider risk to the public."

An IOPC spokesperson said: "After being notified by the Greater Manchester Police of the previous police contact with the parties involved in this incident, we sent investigators to the police post-incident procedures in Manchester in assessment mode to gather further information.

"We continue to remain in assessment mode and will assess a GMP referral in due course."

News.title: Itauma vs Hrgovic LIVE: Fight updates and results tonight as young Briton drops rival to his knees
News.content:
Heavyweight Moses Itauma on why he doesn't like partying as his star rises

Tonight, Moses Itauma has the chance to collect his first world heavyweight title, as he faces Filip Hrgovic in a fascinating main event.

At London’s O2 Arena, Itauma puts his unbeaten record on the line as he aims to pick up the IBF belt, which was recently vacated by Oleksandr Usyk. If the 21-year-old wins, he will become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion ever, after the legendary Mike Tyson.

Itauma isn’t the only one fighting for a full world title for the first time, though. The summit of Hrgovic’s career until now was a 2024 clash with Daniel Dubois, with the interim IBF belt on the line, and the Briton handed the Croat his only professional loss.

Since then, 34-year-old Hrgovic has gone 3-0, with all of those wins coming against British names. Can he add Itauma to the list? Or will the young sensation fulfil his world-title prophecy?

Follow live updates and results from Itauma vs Hrgovic and the undercard, below.

News.title: Fears for communities near the great Colorado River as drought means future is uncertain
News.content:
Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

Located on the outskirts of Phoenix, a small town hugely reliant on the Colorado River has restricted development, reopened disused wells and negotiated new water agreements.

Yet Cave Creek Mayor Robert Morris fears these efforts will prove insufficient to sustain the desert enclave of roughly 5,000 residents long into the future. Furthermore, a recent federal initiative intended to tackle the worsening crisis across the river basin will offer no help.

Cave Creek draws almost all its supply from the river, which provides water to 40 million people across the US West but has been shrinking due to climate change, demand and excessive use. The town was compelled to reduce consumption this year and stands to lose even more under the new federal proposal.

Morris likened the situation to planning for a meteor strike.

“You can see it coming, but you can't get out of the way and you don't know what the damage is going to be,” he said.

open image in gallery A person stands at an overlook near the Wahweap Marina on Lake Powell at the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. )

The uncertainty stretches across seven U.S. states, tribal nations and Mexico. Farmers are deciding which crops are worth the investment. Phoenix could lose some municipal and industrial water for the first time and turn to backup supplies. And residents could face even more costly water.

Nevada raised the stakes this week by suing the Interior Department and the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, saying basic needs in the Las Vegas region will go unmet if the area has to absorb planned reductions of up to 70% of its Colorado River water in the next decade.

The bureau said Thursday it does not comment on litigation.

“The uncertainty is going to continue to build in the wrong direction,” said Tom Buschatzke, director of the Arizona Department of Water Resources.

Western reservoirs see record lows

In the U.S. West, water is stored primarily in reservoirs, aquifers and snowpacks. But a record snow drought means there's far less water to recharge those sources.

The two largest reservoirs in the country serve as barometers of health for the Colorado River system: Lake Mead and Lake Powell. Both hit record lows this month.

Eight other reservoirs operated by the Bureau of Reclamation recently recorded the lowest levels in at least the last 30 years. Among them is Elephant Butte Lake in New Mexico that's critical for supplying water for crops in southern New Mexico, Texas and Mexico. The Green Mountain Reservoir serves the western part of Colorado, and the Guernsey Reservoir in Wyoming funnels water to farmers in the eastern part of the state and western Nebraska.

Under the Bureau of Reclamation’s plan, California, Nevada and Arizona will collectively reduce water use by 1.25 million acre-feet (about 1.54 billion cubic meters) — enough to fill over 600,000 Olympic-sized swimming pools — annually in the next two years, with the possibility of larger cuts depending on conditions. Colorado, Utah, Wyoming and New Mexico are not required to make cuts for now but could voluntarily reduce water.

While El Niño could bring intense moisture to the northern Rockies and the Southwest in the coming months, it won't erase decades of drought.

open image in gallery Tom Brundy looks over his field that is being prepared for planting near Calexico, California ( Copyright 2023 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

“Drought is a slow-moving phenomena and it can take some time to come into it and also come out of it,” said David Mocko, senior research scientist who authored a recent U.S. Drought Monitor map.

Farmers are reluctant to plant

John Boelts grows vegetables, melons, durum wheat and other crops in Yuma, Arizona — a region that produces about 90% of leafy greens eaten in North America during the winter.

Farmers there have high-priority rights and may avoid cuts to their Colorado River supply over the next two years but, Boelts said, the reprieve isn't enough to make longer-term plans. That makes farmers reluctant to plant new acreage.

Citrus, date and other orchard crops that thrive in the region take years to become commercially productive, he said.

“There's no food that we grow in a hurry,” said Boelts, the Arizona Farm Bureau president. “Beef takes years to produce. The lettuce you eat today? A farmer was working on how they would grow that crop six plus months ago.”

Ray Martinez grows alfalfa on a reservation that's home to the Colorado River Indian Tribes. The tribe holds some of the river’s oldest rights, and while its Arizona allocation is huge, an old irrigation system and the lack of infrastructure have kept much of the water out of reach.

Martinez and the water department are concerned about having enough water to finish this growing season. He has left some fields unplanted for years to help prop up Lake Mead. If the reservoir keeps dropping, he said, surface water coming to him and neighboring farms will be further limited.

“Unfortunately, Mother Nature has its own way of doing things, and we have no control of that,” he added.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement plans to spend up to $2 million on robotic “dogs,” according to federal records.

A funding document posted this week by the Department of Homeland Security says the agency could spend between $1 million and $2 million on “SPOT Robots,” which are manufactured by Boston Dynamics.

The robots are intended to assist with “inspection, situational awareness, and hazard assessment in environments that may pose risks to personnel,” according to the planning document.

“This capability helps improve officer safety, supports informed operational decision-making, and enhances DHS’s ability to respond to incidents involving dangerous, confined, unstable, or difficult-to-access areas,” the document adds.

Boston Dynamics, an American robotics company, describes SPOT as an “easy to use” product with “360° perception and athletic intelligence.” The roughly 75-pound, four-legged robot is equipped with cameras and Wi-Fi connectivity and can travel at speeds of up to about 5 feet per second.

open image in gallery Immigrations and Customs Enforcement plans to spend up to $2 million on robot 'dogs' manufactured by Boston Dynamics, according to federal records ( Getty Images )

The machines — which have extendable arms — have already been used by police departments across the U.S., according to ABC News.

The notice comes weeks after DHS published documents indicating that it could spend up to $20 million on specialized gloves capable of delivering painful electric shocks to assist with compliance.

The Independent has contacted DHS for comment.

The department has received a significant influx of funding after President Donald Trump signed the “One Big Beautiful Bill Act” into law last summer. The sweeping legislation, which passed without a single Democratic vote, allocated $165 billion to the department, which oversees ICE.

open image in gallery DHS, which oversees ICE, has received a significant influx of funding after President Donald Trump signed the ‘Big, Beautiful Bill’ into law last summer ( Reuters )

The additional spending comes as many Americans disapprove of Trump’s handling of his anti-immigration campaign. Opposition intensified after two U.S. citizens were killed by federal agents in Minnesota in January.

The president called for a “softer touch” on immigration enforcement following their killings.

Recent data, meanwhile, indicates that ICE has accelerated its enforcement operations. The administration logged its highest monthly totals for immigration-related arrests this summer, with ICE arresting more than 43,000 people in June and another 50,000 in July, The Independent reported this week.

For the first time since Trump took office, more than half of those arrested had no pending criminal charges or prior convictions.

In an August YouGov poll, 53 percent of respondents said they disapproved of Trump’s handling of immigration, while 40 percent approved.

News.title: LA rapper arrested in $8M check-cashing scheme
News.content:
