Sports.title: Alonso gets Chelsea’s priorities right by ditching Sánchez for winner Martínez | Jacob Steinberg
Sports.content:
Carlo Cudicini was a very good goalkeeper. However, José Mourinho was ruthless when he became Chelsea manager in 2004. Very good was not good enough. Mourinho wanted the best and one of the main factors behind the Portuguese winning the Premier League during his first season in charge was the decision to replace Cudicini with Petr Cech.

There is an old line about a great goalkeeper being worth 15 points a season. It is not for nothing, for instance, that Brian Clough regarded Peter Shilton as one of his most important signings at Nottingham Forest. Shilton was key when Forest defied the odds by winning the Division One title in 1978 and there are plenty of other examples of promising teams taking the next step only after buying a top No 1.

Jürgen Klopp’s Liverpool did not become the finished article until signing Alisson in 2018, while Arsenal might not have finished top last season without David Raya’s crucial save during the 1-0 win over West Ham in May. Chelsea, though, developed a blind spot after selling Thibaut Courtois to Real Madrid eight years ago.

A host of inconsistent goalkeepers have come and gone, or in some cases stuck around long after it became clear they were not a patch on Cech and Courtois, and it is only now that Chelsea have tackled the issue head on.

The £7.5m signing of Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa adds to the sense that this will go down as the summer when BlueCo got serious. The focus on youth remains but has lowered in intensity and the decision to ditch Robert Sánchez after his clumsy performance during last Monday’s 3-2 win over Fulham shows that Xabi Alonso will not hesitate to make the big calls.

The only frustration for supporters is that it has taken this long for Chelsea to give up on Sánchez, three years after signing him from Brighton for £25m. There have been occasional challenges but none have lasted. Mauricio Pochettino switched to Djordje Petrovic midway through the 2023-24 season, only for Enzo Maresca to return to Sánchez after becoming Chelsea’s head coach in the summer of 2024.

Filip Jörgensen, signed from Villarreal as Sánchez’s deputy two years ago, then had chances to establish himself as the No 1. Jörgensen is better than Sánchez with his feet but struggled to convince. Maresca did not stick with the Dane after bringing him into the side in February 2025. The turning point in Liam Rosenior’s brief reign came when his decision to select Jörgensen over Sanchez in a Champions League tie against Paris Saint-Germain last season backfired so badly that Chelsea lost 5-2.

Jörgensen departed this summer and it seemed that Chelsea were going to ignore all the outsiders who insisted that Sánchez also had to go. The message was that Alonso was happy with his options in goal. Sánchez was going to remain as the No 1 and the academy graduate Teddy Sharman-Lowe was third choice, while part of the thinking behind the club’s refusal to go into the market for a new goalkeeper was their belief that Mike Penders is going to become one of the best in the world.

Penders, who made his debut in the Carabao Cup win over Luton on Thursday, joined from Genk for £17m two years ago. Chelsea’s determination not to block the 21-year-old Belgian’s pathway partly explains why they have not pursued opportunities to sign Milan’s Mike Maignan and Porto’s Diogo Costa during the past two summers.

This was supposed to be a season of gradual change. Sánchez was still first pick but was going to face healthy competition from Penders. Both were content with that situation. Ben Roberts, Chelsea’s head of goalkeeping, worked with Sánchez at Brighton and has long been one of his biggest advocates.

Yet Sánchez’s performance against Fulham forced Chelsea’s hand. It was clear that there was not going to be a title challenge unless a new goalkeeper was signed before Tuesday’s transfer deadline. The proof was overwhelming. Sánchez dribbled the ball behind for a corner at one point and was at fault for both Fulham goals. He spread anxiety, making his defenders nervous, and Alonso knew it was time to act.

Things moved quickly when Chelsea were contacted by Martínez’s representatives earlier this week. The club’s sporting leadership presented the idea to Alonso, who gave them the green light, and the transfer was completed on Thursday night.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea believe 21-year-old Mike Penders can become one of the best goalkeepers in the world. Photograph: Chris Lee/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

There was some doubt about whether it would be a permanent deal. Some people wondered if a loan would make more sense, ensuring this was a temporary fix rather than one to spook Penders.

More pressingly, meanwhile, there were warnings about Sánchez’s mood. There was concern over whether the 28-year-old would accept an immediate demotion. Yet Chelsea have not worried about hurt feelings. There is little time to act but Sánchez needs to leave. He will be frozen out if he stays and looks unlikely to feature when Chelsea host Brighton on Sunday. There is interest from clubs in England, Europe and Saudi Arabia.

This is life at the top. Chelsea have been decisive. Sánchez is capable of wondrous saves, can command his area and is liked in the dressing room, but he is shaky with his feet and prone to calamitous games. Chelsea needed stability. They watched Pochettino, Maresca and Rosenior change goalkeeper during the season. It is better to have a clear hierarchy from the start.

Enter Martínez, who has long been looking for a way out of Villa. He almost joined Manchester United last summer and recently appeared to be on his way to Juventus. Villa have moved on, signing Zion Suzuki. Martínez has been a great servant but wanted a new challenge. Chelsea assessed the conditions of a deal. Martínez had other offers but wanted to play for Alonso. That desire convinced Chelsea to do the deal.

It makes sense. Martínez is 34 next week and has signed on a two-year deal, with the option of an extra year. Penders has an experienced mentor. He can continue to grow and knows his time will come.

Chelsea are focused on the present. Martinez has a winning mentality – he is Argentina’s No 1 and a World Cup winner in 2022 – and has been one of the best goalkeepers in England since joining Villa from Arsenal in 2020. There is still no guarantee Chelsea will challenge Arsenal’s dominance but they surely have a better chance with Martínez in goal.

Sports.title: Hull maintain flying start as Liam Millar’s winner ruins Coventry’s day
Sports.content:
Perhaps last Saturday’s triumph was not a one-off. Hull backed up a shock victory against Manchester United by maintaining their 100% start to the Premier League and condemning Coventry to successive defeats. “We’re gonna win the league,” was the glorious chant raining down from the Hull support after Liam Millar’s 82nd-minute strike.

The goal was a sucker punch for Coventry, who were pushing for a winner and looked set to claim at least their first point of the season. Frank Lampard, arms folded, was unmoved as the away end rejoiced.

He and Coventry may wonder where their first point – and, indeed, their first goal – will come from. Next is a daunting trip to Manchester City, before they host Brighton, who began the season with a 4-0 trouncing of Aston Villa. Hull, as they did last season, are exceeding all expectations.

Was losing to another promoted team, one who finished 22 points behind them last season, a mental blow? “It depends how much you want it to be,” Lampard said. “There are 36 games left; we’re two games in. It depends how you react to a defeat.”

For Coventry, as their owner and chair, Doug King, said beforehand, a first Premier League for more than 25 years was a historic day for the city. “I know how much it means to all of us,” he said, this also their first top-flight game in this stadium.

The buzz before kick-off was palpable, none more so than when King – wearing an elephant brooch on his suit, the animal that adorns Coventry’s badge and the city’s coat of arms – joined Coventry supporters in singing along to The Enemy’s We’ll Live and Die in These Towns, the club’s adopted prematch anthem. The pyrotechnics left a haze drifting across the pitch as things got under way.

At full time, it was down to Millar and Sergej Jakirovic, albeit after a little persuading, to conduct the Hull celebrations. “It gives us big confidence as a team, individuals, for me as well, because I don’t have experience at this level,” said Hull’s head coach. “We have a lot of work to do, we need to keep our feet on the ground and stay humble. We know our target: 38, 41 points? We will see.”

View image in fullscreen Liam Millar slots the ball away in the 82nd minute to win Hull the game. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

Both teams lacked quality, but Coventry were undeniably the more threatening side. Taiwo Awoniyi, on his full league debut for the club, sent a weak header at Konstantinos Tzolakis and later forced the Hull goalkeeper into a smart right-hand save after Loum Tchaouna’s cross skidded off the head of Nobel Mendy. Lampard cycled through substitutions, the arrival of Gustavo Hamer, something of a hero in these parts, lifting the home crowd, but they struggled to work Tzolakis.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Millar, who arrived on the hour, had wasted Hull’s best opening with 74 minutes on the clock, Jakirovic wearing a look of disgust after the Canada winger ignored an unmarked Mohamed Belloumi to his right and sent his shot bobbling wide after a clever first-time pass by Oli McBurnie released Millar behind Bobby Thomas. Until then, their only shot on target was Mendy’s speculative shot from 30 yards.

But Millar made amends, coolly slotting past Carl Rushworth to cap a devastating counterattack. Victor Torp’s attempted cross from the left boomeranged off Lucas Gourna-Douath and into midfield, where Belloumi overpowered Tatsuhiro Sakamoto and sent Millar streaming into the opposition half with a sumptuous outside-of-the-boot pass.

“I think Millar was a bit disappointed with the first chance but then showed massive bollocks to score the second,” McBurnie said. “As a striker, it’s not the one you want when you’ve just missed a chance: you’ve got to run 40 yards and then think about your shot. You’ve got too much time to think.”

Twelve months ago, Hull were reeling from back-to-back defeats against Blackburn and Bristol City and adapting to life under a transfer embargo. They made up for lost time this summer with Mohamed Ali-Cho, who made his debut late on here, and another forward, Ilyas Ansah, a £20m buy from Union Berlin, their 12th and 13th arrivals of the window respectively.

“We knew this was going to be a really tough game, in some ways even tougher than last week,” McBurnie said. “Considering we’re ‘the worst team in Premier League history’, it’s not a bad start from the boys.”

Sports.title: Three Tottenham players ask to leave as Roberto De Zerbi makes bombshell announcement
Sports.content:
Three Tottenham players ask to leave as Roberto De Zerbi makes bombshell announcement

Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr have all asked to leave Tottenham Hotspur, Roberto De Zerbi has confirmed.

The trio were not part of the squad that lost 2-0 to Newcastle United on Saturday evening.

3 Richarlison is looking to leave Spurs this summer Credit: Getty

Richarlison and Danso have each played one match out of a possible three this season, while Sarr has not featured at all.

De Zerbi was asked about his squad during his post-Newcastle press conference and revealed their wishes to leave the club.

"Richarlison, he's said too many times he wants to leave," the Spurs head coach said.

"Danso came to me two days ago, and he said he wants to leave.

"The other player, Sarr, is the same but he's suffered a small injury. But, he's almost ready to train."

De Zerbi then responded to a question about whether or not he had a message for the players, and if they had a way back into the team.

"I love these players, and they are great guys," the Italian explained. "I have very good relationships.

"But, if they want to leave, they have to bring the economic solution to the club and they can go, and we'll find other players."

Richarlison, Danso and Sarr eye exit

With the transfer window closing on Tuesday, the wantaway trio still have time to find new clubs.

Spurs have signed Omar Marmoush from Manchester City, with the deal including an initial season-long loan and £60million obligation.

3 Danso is also keen to depart the club Credit: Getty

His arrival may well have increased Richarlison's chances of leaving as he is in the final months of his contract.

Richarlison has been underwhelming for Spurs since his £60m move from Everton in 2022, having scored 32 goals in 134 appearances.

The forward started in the defeat at Brentford, but did not have a single shot on target across 68 minutes.

Danso is reportedly of interest to Premier League rivals Sunderland, who have had a loan bid rejected.

Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi are two players to have joined Spurs this summer as new centre-back options.

Micky van de Ven, who was captain against Newcastle, is seemingly top of the pecking order, while Danso has dropped down.

3 Sarr is another player who is looking to move away from Spurs Credit: Getty

Galatasaray, Aston Villa and Juventus have all been linked with Sarr.

However, AS Monaco are said to be leading the race for the midfielder ahead of the transfer deadline.

Sports.title: Championship boss at risk of sack after just three league wins since start of January
Sports.content:
Championship boss at risk of sack after just three league wins since start of January

Mark Robins faces increased pressure as Stoke City boss, talkSPORT understands.

The Potters have won just three matches in the Championship since January 2026.

2 Robins has overseen a dismal run of form at Stoke Credit: Getty

Stoke have lost all of their opening three fixtures this season, with a 4-1 defeat away to Wolves on Saturday their most recent result.

Robins joined the former Premier League club in January 2025 after he was dismissed by Coventry City.

He secured their Championship survival by finishing 18th, and Stoke then ended the following campaign one place higher.

However, they are rock-bottom of the table with a goal difference of -6 - the worst out of all 24 teams.

Premier League exile to continue at Stoke

Stoke made their Premier League debut in the 2008/09 season and even managed to finish 12th as they steered clear of the drop.

During their ten-season stay in England's top flight, the Potters also competed in the Europa League.

However, by finishing 19th in the 2017/18 campaign, they were sent back down to the Championship, where they have remained since.

They have never finished higher than 14th in the second tier, and so a return to the Premier League looks distant.

Stoke have not played in League One since the 2001/02 season when they competed in what as then known as the Division Two.

But as it stands, relegation cannot be ruled out this season.

2 Stoke has lost all three of their league matches this season Credit: Getty

What's next for Stoke?

Following defeats to Swansea City, Southampton and Wolves, Stoke will look to bag their first points on Tuesday night.

They host Norwich City, who were 4-1 winners over Burnley in their weekend fixture.

Another home match against table-toppers Charlton Athletic follows, and then it's a trip to Cardiff City.

Watford and Sheffield United are their final opponents before the first international break of the season.

Stoke return on October 10 when they travel to Bolton Wanderers.

Sports.title: Cody Gakpo makes next club decision amid Man City and Tottenham transfer battle
Sports.content:
Man City have made an opening bid for Cody Gakpo and the player wants to join them, talkSPORT understands.

Gakpo started, and got an assist, in Liverpool's 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

3 Gakpo has started Liverpool's opening two games, despite transfer interest elsewhere Credit: Getty

However, with Bradley Barcola coming into the club there has been speculation over his future.

Tottenham have been the club showing most interest in Gakpo this summer.

But now City have ramped up their pursuit of the Dutch international in recent days.

talkSPORT understands Man City are in formal talks with Liverpool and an opening bid has already been made.

The £85m fee, £75m and £10m in add-ons, City received for Savio is likely to be used as a benchmark in negotiations.

There is optimism if the total package reaches this number then a deal will get done.

Cody Gakpo to City latest

talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs said: “Manchester City in the last few days have gone really big on Cody Gakpo. It's taken the player a little bit by surprise because for much of the summer, it was Tottenham and Cody Gakpo. He’d spoken to Roberto De Zerbi.

“But our information is that Cody Gakpo favours Manchester City.

“As a consequence, this is expected to develop. I actually think that Tottenham now realise they can't do that deal. Do they turn to Iliman Ndiaye as a result?

“Bradley Barcola comes in, as we exclusively revealed this morning, for £106m with £17m in add-ons.

3 Iraola could have a busy last few days of the window Credit: Getty

“It may come down to the player realising even if they don't add now another attacker, Victor Munoz has come in and Rio Ngumoha needs a pathway.

"Gakpo maybe in previous seasons could have looked out wide, looked in the centre. But now up front, it's Alexander Isak and Hugo Ekitike. Behind them, it's Florian Wirtz.

“So I think he seems to believe that even if it's not now, it might be the beginning of the end.

“This was kind of what Luis Diaz thought when Liverpool wanted to keep the player, but eventually they sold him to Bayern Munich.

“Cody Gakpo has got a big decision to make. From Liverpool's perspective, if they were to sell, they know they're bringing in more money.

“It might mean that they can overpay for an Ismaïla Sarr or a Yankuba Minteh. Then two attackers will come in as well.”

3 Gakpo is a Premier League winner with Liverpool Credit: AFP

The 27-year-old signed for Liverpool from PSV in 2023 for around £44m.

He signed a new long-term contract with the club last summer.

Gakpo also has 51 goals in 182 games in all competitions for the club.

More Liverpool signings?

Asked by talkSPORT's Sam Matterface after his side's 2-2 home draw with Nottingham Forest whether he'd be happy with his squad should the Barcola deal go through, Iraola said: "I think now we need to be patient. We don't know what's going to happen.

"There are still some days [left] in the market and obviously there are going to be movements. We will need to analyse when this happens.

"I'm looking forward to being in the second half of September and knowing what we have, and then making definitive plans with this.

"But the competition works like this – the rules are the same for everyone.

"It's uncomfortable in terms of uncertainty until the market closes, but now it's just a matter of a couple of days, so we will wait."

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest attempt double Crystal Palace raid after £22m Daniel Munoz deal agreed
Sports.content:
Add us as preferred source

Nottingham Forest have sent a bid for Crystal Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson, talkSPORT understands.

New Forest boss Oliver Glasner is attempting to raid his old club for a second time this summer.



3 Henderson is the subject of an offer from former loan club Nottingham Forest Credit: Getty

Glasner left Palace at the end of the 2025/26 season after winning the Conference League.

Forest have agreed a £22m fee for defender Daniel Munoz.

Now England goalkeeper Henderson is in their sights.

However, talkSPORT understands Palace consider him not for sale.

The East Midlands club are searching for a new goalkeeper before the transfer window closes on Tuesday.

Matz Sels started for the 2-2 draw with Liverpool on Saturday.

Henderson is Crystal Palace's current club captain, having joined from Manchester United on a permanent deal in 2023.



The 29-year-old also played 20 games for Forest in the 2022/23 season while on loan from United.

Daniel Munoz deal

Colombia international Munoz has been given permission to undergo a medical at Forest.



The 30-year-old has two years left on his contract at Selhurst Park.

He won the FA Cup and Conference League with Palace under Glasner.

3 Forest will sign Munoz for £22m Credit: Getty

Munoz has made 109 appearances for Palace, scoring 11 goals, and played in their opening 2-0 Premier League defeat.



He was then an unused substitute in their defeat to Man City on Friday.

Forest want Harrison Armstrong

Nottingham Forest have also launched an ambitious bid for Everton teenage midfielder Harrison Armstrong.

The Toffees are prepared to sell the 19-year-old, with Forest offering £40m.

Oliver Glasner verdict

Speaking to talkSPORT after the draw with Liverpool, Glasner said: "I could see many positive signs, many positive aspects in the game.



"Defensively, attacking wise, how many chances we created, scoring the first two goals for us.

3 Forest drew 2-2 with Liverpool at Anfield on Saturday Credit: Getty

“The first Premier League game against Leeds was very tight and we had the small margins on their side.

“I think the cup game was not our best performance, but we learned from it.



“We are learning from every single game right now and this game today will also help us in growing.

“I think the performance especially gives us a lot of confidence for the season.”

Forest are next in action against Tottenham on Saturday, September 5.

Sports.title: Tottenham star brutally told he’s not good enough after ‘one of worst free kicks in history’
Sports.content:
Tottenham star brutally told he’s not good enough after ‘one of worst free kicks in history’

Jamie O'Hara believes Mathys Tel is not up to standard at Tottenham Hotspur after his disastrous free kick.

The forward was tasked with taking the set piece as Spurs trailed 1-0 in their 2-0 home defeat to Newcastle United on Saturday evening.



3 Tel had a moment to forget against Newcastle Credit: Getty

He blazed his effort high above the Newcastle defence and into the South Stand at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

O'Hara was watching live on GameDay Phone-In for talkSPORT and did not hold back on his assessment of the free kick.

"Oh my word! It's one of the worst free kicks I've ever seen," the ex-Spurs man declared.



His co-host Jason Cundy revelled in the miss, and jibed: "By the way, that might have left the stadium."

O'Hara then added: "Listen, I didn't want to say it because he was standing over the free kick and if he bends it into the top corner, then it would have been a shambles.



"But, he's not good enough. I don't know why everyone's going on like he's a decent player, he's absolutely guff."

Spurs fan JJ agreed with O'Hara as he called in to say: "I tell you what, the player that needs to get right out of this team is Mathys Tel.



"His decision-making is guff, right? That's one of the things that should be paramount for a footballer, is your decision-making."

Tel was eventually substituted by Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi as he looked for a way back into the match.

But moments later, Newcastle scored their second with an acrobatic finish from Yoane Wissa.

3 Newcastle were deserved winners in north London Credit: Getty



Bad to worse for Spurs

After deservedly losing 3-0 to Brentford on the opening weekend, Spurs had a great opportunity to pick up their first points at home.

They came into the match against Newcastle off the back of a 5-1 win against Charlton Athletic in the Carabao Cup second round.

However, despite hitting the £300million mark on new signings this summer, they were nothing but woeful.

Anthony Elanga scored a brilliant goal on the turn with just over an hour played to fire Newcastle in front.



Wissa then wrapped up the three points in the 72nd minute as Spurs' players continued their lack of cutting edge going forward.

After 180 minutes of Premier League football this season, they have conceded five goals and scored none.

3 Spurs are back in the Premier League relegation zone Credit: Getty

It's also the first time that Spurs have lost their opening two matches in a Premier League season without scoring.



They sit bottom of the table and, as things stand, could be involved in yet another scrap against a shock relegation.

Sports.title: Why VAR could not intervene as Liverpool fans furious with Liam Delap ‘foul throw’
Sports.content:
Why VAR could not intervene as Liverpool fans furious with Liam Delap ‘foul throw’

A former Premier League referee has explained why the VAR couldn't intervene with an apparent foul throw from Liam Delap.

The Nottingham Forest debutant played a key role in their second goal during the 2-2 draw with Liverpool on Saturday afternoon.

3 Gibbs-White put Forest in front after Williams won a penalty from Delap's throw-in Credit: Getty

Delap, who has signed from Chelsea in a deal worth up to £50million, delivered a throw into the path of Neco Williams.

He was fouled by goalkeeper Alisson and Morgan Gibbs-White scored the resulting penalty to put Forest ahead at Anfield.

However, Liverpool fans have taken issue with Delap's throw-in as he appeared to breach International Football Association Board (IFAB) rules.

They state that the thrower must face the field of play and throw the ball behind and over their head with both hands.

Throwers must also have a part of each foot on the the touchline, or on the ground outside of it, for the throw-in to be eligible.

Having looked at replays, Liverpool fans on social media pointed out that Delap seemingly had one foot off the touchline when throwing.

"The most blatant foul throw you’ll ever see from Liam Delap," said one on X, as another added: "Unsure why it wasn't checked.

A third asked: "Was I the only one who thought that was a foul throw from Delap leading to the pen?"

Why could VAR not intervene with Delap's throw-in?

Despite this, the penalty stood, and Graham Scott has explained why the match officials could not step in and overrule the decision.

"The VAR protocol does not allow it," Scott, who refereed 107 Premier League matches, said in a post on X.

3 Referee Samuel Barrott awarded the penalty and VAR did not review the throw-in Credit: Getty

"In any event, it appears the thrower's foot only comes off the ground after release, which would make the throw-in legal.

"Whether it's a pen is another matter."

Liverpool and Forest share the points

Forest were the more impressive side in the first half and found the opener on 24 minutes via Dan Ndoye.

Florian Wirtz had an equaliser ruled out for offside, but Liverpool eventually drew level thanks to Alexander Isak with an hour played.

The throw-in controversy followed a few minutes later and Gibbs-White looked to be sending Forest towards all three points.

But Victor Munoz scored the hosts' second equalising goal of the afternoon eight minutes from time.

3 An explanation as to why VAR could not step in has been given Credit: Getty

Speaking to talkSPORT after full-time, Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola hinted at more signings before the transfer deadline on September 1.

They are understood to have agreed a package worth £123m to sign Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain.

Sports.title: Nuno Espirito Santo responds to brutal West Ham fan chants after Championship clash
Sports.content:
Nuno Espirito Santo has asked for West Ham fans to get behind the team after they called for him to be sacked.

The Hammers are still winless after three Championship games, drawing at Watford on Saturday.



2 West Ham fans have called for Nuno Espirito Santo to be sacked Credit: Getty

They currently sit 19th with just two points to their name since dropping down from the Premier League.

West Ham fans were quick to voice their fury with a section of supporters chanting ‘you’re getting sacked in the morning’.

The Hammers stuck by Nuno this summer, despite being widely expected to part ways with the Portuguese at the end of last season.



The club were forced to release a statement confirming he would remain in charge.

Nuno on West Ham fan chants

Speaking to talkSPORT’s Ben Jacobs after the game, the West Ham boss said: “I understand. It's true, the results are not coming, but we have to support ourselves, try to remain together.



"The support of the fans are essential for us to play better, for the boys to show all the talent that they have on the pitch.

“Once again, I ask them to keep supporting and helping us.”

When asked if he feels under pressure, Nuno replied: “We have pressure every day at West Ham. We are a huge club.



“Even the players that joined us realised that we have to perform better and the fans have to be happy. We only achieve that with wins.

“This is what we are chasing.”

2 West Ham are still winless in the Championship Credit: Getty

West Ham’s performance

West Ham dominated the ball against Watford, but managed just three shots on target in the whole game.

Amin Nabizada’s opener for the Hornets was cancelled out by a Mattie Pollock own goal, which was initially attributed to Taty Castellanos.



Nuno believes his side should have got more out of each of the three games they have played so far.

He added: “We have to go back and see all the games. The first game of the season was Burnley, we had Charlton, which was disappointing. Today, again disappointing.

“If you look back, we feel that all of the games we should have done better and achieved a different result.”

Next up for West Ham is Wolves at the London Stadium on Tuesday night.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola hints at more Liverpool transfers before window slams shut on Tuesday
Sports.content:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has hinted at more transfer activity in the final days of the window.

Deadline day falls on Tuesday (September 1) and the Reds could yet do more business, with Bradley Barcola firmly in their sights.



2 Liverpool have Barcola firmly in their sights Credit: Getty

Indeed, talkSPORT understands Liverpool have agreed a package worth up to £123m for the Paris Saint-Germain winger.

Iraola: 'We must be patient'

Asked by talkSPORT's Sam Matterface after his side's 2-2 home draw with Nottingham Forest whether he'd be happy with his squad should the Barcola deal go through, Iraola said: "I think now we need to be patient. We don't know what's going to happen.

"There are still some days [left] in the market and obviously there are going to be movements. We will need to analyse when this happens.



"I'm looking forward to being in the second half of September and knowing what we have, and then making definitive plans with this.

"But the competition works like this – the rules are the same for everyone.



"It's uncomfortable in terms of uncertainty until the market closes, but now it's just a matter of a couple of days, so we will wait."

With regards to the uncertainty Iraola speaks of, Cody Gakpo's Liverpool future is still up in the air.



The winger has been linked with both Tottenham and Manchester City, and his manager admitted he couldn't be sure if he would remain a Reds player beyond the transfer window.

No Gakpo guarantees

At his press conference ahead of the Forest last, Iraola said: "I can say what I said last week, and even after the performance he had in the first game.

"He is playing very well for us. He has been very good since he came back from the World Cup and after the holidays, a good attitude and I hope we can keep him at that level because he has been very influential.

2 Gakpo has started both of Liverpool's games so far this season Credit: Getty



"When the market is open you cannot guarantee anything with anyone. When I arrived I would like to know how the market finishes and then when you finish with this one and this one, but I don't know what is going to happen with any of our players. I cannot guarantee anything.

"You think I can smell who we are going to sign or what position, but experience shows you that, if there is an opportunity on the last day [of the transfer window], let's take it."

Gakpo started again on Saturday, setting up Liverpool's first equaliser through Alexander Isak – who, despite scoring, was criticised for his 'flat' performance at Anfield.

But Barcola's arrival would surely see Gakpo drop out of the starting 11, given the France international's preferred side is also the left.



What's next for Liverpool?

Liverpool, still looking for their first win under Iraola, return to Premier League action away to Ipswich next Friday, live on talkSPORT.

They then get their Champions League campaign underway at home to Atletico Madrid the following Wednesday.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi reveals THREE Spurs stars have told him they want to leave as he warns solution needs to be found as transfer deadline nears
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi reveals THREE Spurs stars have told him they want to leave as he warns solution needs to be found as transfer deadline nears

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roberto De Zerbi has revealed that Pape Matar Sarr, Richarlison and Kevin Danso were all left out of Tottenham’s matchday squad to take on Newcastle after asking to leave the club.

De Zerbi also apologised to Tottenham fans after his side were beaten 2-0 by Newcastle to leave Spurs bottom of the Premier League.

‘Richarlison he said too many times that he wanted to leave,’ De Zerbi said. ‘Danso came to me two days ago and said he wanted to leave. Sarr the same but he also suffered a small injury but he is almost ready to train.

‘I love these players and these are great guys. I have very good relationships but if they want to leave they have to bring the economic solution to the club and they can go and we’ll find other players.’

Spurs finished 17th last term, surviving by two points and now sit bottom of the division after two games, shipping five goals without reply.

De Zerbi’s side have spent close to £400million this summer with former Newcastle midfielder Sandro Tonali and Omar Marmoush among those brought to the club.

Richarlison is one of three Spurs players who wants to leave the club, Roberto De Zerbi said

Join the discussion Which Tottenham players will leave before Deadline Day?

‘I’m disappointed by the result and sorry to the fans for the environment after two defeats — maybe somebody thinks it’s the same history as the last two seasons,’ De Zerbi said.

‘I have no doubt it’s not like this. I can’t change my opinion after two defeats. I have big, big confidence in the qualities of my players. I’m sorry for the club. They are building a great squad but maybe they are not ready for many reasons.

‘Until the first goal we played better than Newcastle. More shots, more control of the ball, we suffered in two or three situations in the first half because distances too big, then after the goal we lost confidence and the reaction was not good enough, not the reaction I want to see on the pitch.’

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle took plenty of positives away from his first victory at the club, which follows last weekend’s home draw with Liverpool.

‘It was incredible and I’m really proud,’ said Jaissle. ‘We are really proud as a club, as a coaching staff, to see a team on the pitch delivering the match plan at a high level already, but also seeing players fully committed to what we’re doing.

‘This is a good start and a moment to enjoy.’

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola set for Liverpool medical in next 24 hours ahead of £123m move to Premier League club: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest agree £22m deal for Daniel Munoz and bid for Dean Henderson, Man City open talks for Cody Gakpo, Fiorentina chase Leeds' Willy Gnonto... and Juventus close on deal for Pape Matar Sarr: WINDOW WATCH

For yesterday's developments - including Atletico setting a deadline for Julian Alvarez to decide on a move to Arsenal - click HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Chelsea working on two midfielders amid Enzo drama

Chelsea are still working on recruiting two midfielders should Manchester City prise away Enzo Fernandez before Tuesday’s deadline.

Chelsea are expecting a formal approach from City for the Argentine, who was left out of the matchday squad against Luton.

Manager Xabi Alonso explained his absence by saying: ‘We need players that are in the best situation to play. We need to take everything into consideration — players that are in a good moment, players that are not feeling that energy to play. For me, it is very important they feel this desire to play and to have good preparation.’

Leeds land Zetterer

Leeds United have signed goalkeeper Michael Zetterer from Eintracht Frankfurt in a permanent transfer.

The deal is worth £4.2m for the 31-year-old, who will be James Trafford's deputy.

Zetterer has joined Leeds on a three-year contract. He is replacing Lucas Perri who joined Torino on loan.

Michael Zetterer is on his way to Elland Road in a deal worth £4.2m

Tigers try to catch ANOTHER player

Hull City have made an ambitious offer for Eintracht Frankfurt's highly-rated French winger Jean-Matteo Bahoya.

The 21-year-old, has interest from a number of clubs. He is the only player in Bundesliga history to surpass 37km/h since records began. Usain Bolt’s average speed when he set his 100m world record in 2009 was 37.58km/h.

Villa offer Maatsen new deal after United interest

Aston Villa are to offer left back Ian Maatsen, 24, a new contract after Manchester United explored his potential availability before the deadline.

City open talks over Gakpo - who wants to join

Manchester City have opened talks with Liverpool for Cody Gakpo.

The Netherlands international has intimated he would rather join City over rival interest from Tottenham.

Formal negotiations began on Saturday evening with City aware that Liverpool would require a substantial fee.

Liverpool had earlier agreed to sign Bradley Barcola for £123m and remain determined to add another forward before Tuesday's deadline.

Cody Gakpo has told Liverpool he wants to join Manchester City over Tottenham

Juve close to deal for Sarr

Juventus are closing on a deal for Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr.

The Italians are offering a loan with obligation to buy the Senegal international.

The 23-year-old has had offers from Monaco, Nottingham Forest and Besiktas but Juventus are now in pole position.

Roberto De Zerbi confirmed Sarr, Richarlison, and Kevin Danso had asked to leave the club. Spurs rejected a loan offer from Danso from Sunderland though Aston Villa have interest.

Forest bid for Henderson... as Hutchinson sets sights on Milan

Nottingham Forest have made a bid for Crystal Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson, hours after sealing a fee for his team-mate Daniel Munoz. Oliver Glasner is keen to link up with the England international. AC Milan, meanwhile, are closing on agreement for Nottingham Forest winger Omari Hutchinson. The 22-year-old is ready to join on loan with the deal becoming an obligation based on certain conditions.

Dean Henderson is subject of a bid from Nottingham Forest and his old boss Oliver Glasner

Hammers in for Austbo

West Ham are in talks to sign Viking winger Edvin Austbo for £18million.

Austbo, 21, has scored 15 goals across 71 appearances since making his debut for the Norwegian champions in 2022.

Fiorentina chasing Gnonto

Fiorentina are in talks with Leeds United over a deal for winger Willy Gnonto. However, Leeds will not allow Gnonto to leave without finding a replacement first. They have been keen to sign Mykhailo Mudryk from Chelsea and are expected to try again before the end of the window.

Everton fans plea over Armstrong

Everton travelling supporters made their feelings clear on Harrison Armstrong’s potential sale to Nottingham Forest. At today's Premier League clash at Bournemouth fans in the away end repeatedly chanted: 'Don’t sell Armstrong, Harrison Armstrong, I just don’t think you understand.... If you sell Armstrong, Harrison Armstrong, you’re going to have a riot on your hands.'

Armstrong, 19, is a £40m target for Nottingham Forest and started the game. It is understood other clubs are interested if Everton do agree to sell.

Everton have gone back to Fulham over Kenny Tete, who turned them down to stay at Craven Cottage last year. Fulham are in talks to sign right back Andrei Ratiu from Rayo Vallecano.

Talks are continuing over a deal for the 28-year-old Romania defender. Tete was a target for Everton a year ago but turned them down. He is one of a couple of options they are trying.

Harrison Armstrong in action for Everton at Bournemouth this afternoon

Munoz set for Forest in £22m deal

Daniel Munoz is set to complete a move to Nottingham Forest after the club agreed a deal in principle with Crystal Palace.

The Colombian international, a favourite of Oliver Glasner, is set to link up with his old boss at the City Ground for a fee of about £22million.

Munoz was a key player in the Glasner era at Selhurst Park, when the Eagles won three trophies. But at 30, Palace believe this is a good deal ahead of the transfer window closing on September 1.

Forest drew 2-2 at Liverpool today and are keen to strengthen in midfield, with talks underway to sign Harrison Armstrong from Everton for about £40m.

As revealed by Daily Mail Sport, Forest are also prepared to let winger Omari Hutchinson depart after leaving him out of the squad at Anfield. AC Milan have shown a strong interest in the England Under-21 international and if talks proceed smoothly, he could fly to Italy as soon as Sunday.

Discussions between the clubs have centred around an initial season-long loan deal with an obligation to buy if certain conditions are met. Milan are managed by former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim and have started the season with two wins.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Daniel Munoz is set to move to Nottingham Forest

Gunners snap up United winger

Arsenal have announced the signing of winger James Scanlon from Manchester United. The deal is a free transfer but United retain a 50 per cent sell-on.

The 19-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at League Two side Swindon Town, where he scored his first senior club goal and helped the Robins finish ninth. However, he was viewed as having little chance of making an impact on United’s first team.

Scanlon is already a Gibraltar international, earning 24 senior caps and featuring in World Cup qualifiers and Nations League matches.

'I can’t wait to get started,' Scanlon told the club’s official website. 'I’ve been waiting to get this over the line, so I’m buzzing to be here.'

Arsenal have also agreed a deal to sign 17-year-old Georgian attacking midfielder Andria Bartishvili ahead of Paris Saint-Germain.

The teenager is due to have a medical next week before joining in the New Year.

James Scanlon already has plenty of international experience with Gibraltar

United academy star heads for Rotherham loan

Manchester United academy midfielder Jayce Fitzgerald is set to join Rotherham United on loan.

Daily Mail Sport understands the 19-year-old, who has never previously been out on loan, is keen to test himself in a senior set-up after excelling at Under-21s level.

Fitzgerald will head to Rotherham, the club who helped develop fellow Manchester United youngster Dan Gore last season. Gore won their Player of the Season award.

NATHAN SALT

Jayce Fitzgerald, here in Manchester United training, is taking his first steps in senior football

Foxes on the hunt

Leicester City, who visit MK Dons in League One today, want to sign either George Dobson or Matty James from Wrexham and are asking about both midfielders.

Wrexham are still in for Leicester centre back Harry Souttar as they juggle targets.

City's Bah talks over move to Germany

Manchester City centre back Juma Bah is in talks to join Augsburg on loan.

The 20-year-old 6ft 5in defender spent last season on loan at Nice.

Leeds try Harder ahead of deadline

Leeds United maintain an interest in RB Leipzig forward Conrad Harder though they face competition for the Denmark international.

Leipzig are finalising a deal for Chelsea's Marc Guiu to increase competition for places. Leeds winger Willy Gnonto is attracting attention from Fiorentina meanwhile.

The winger has missed Leeds' first two games of the season with a hamstring injury he sustained during pre-season.

Conrad Harder is subject of interest from several clubs, including Leeds

Black Cats enquire about Malick

Sunderland have asked about Lyon winger Malick Fofana.

The 21-year-old has been discussing a move to Roma but Sunderland have made a late check as their own pursuit of a winger has hit a few bumps.

They remain in talks for Igor Paixao from Marseille and had placed an offer for Geny Catamo at Sporting Lisbon but have still to reach breakthrough.

They also enquired for Manchester City's Jack Grealish earlier this week but believe he may end up at Tottenham.

Besiktas ask about Sarr

Besiktas have asked about signing Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr on a permanent deal.

The Senegal international also has Monaco and Nottingham Forest offers to consider

Elliott a target for Valencia

Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott is being eyed by Spanish side Valencia.

As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, the 23-year-old has interest from a number of clubs with Lazio and Napoli among them but Valencia are hopeful they can sign the England U21 international on loan.

Liverpool have still to receive an official approach but are aware of interest.

Harvey Elliott was not part of Liverpool's squad for the clash with Nottingham Forest today

Malaga push for Everton's Aznou

Malaga are progressing in talks to sign Adam Aznou from Everton.

Aznou came on as a substitute in the 4-0 win over Preston North End in midweek but has struggled since joining from Bayern Munich.

Everton have checked on Melvin Bard at Nice, among others.

Toon press on with Pardo move

Newcastle United are continuing to discuss a move for Lille forward Mathias-Fernandez Pardo and appreciate Bilal El Khannouss at Stuttgart.

El Khannouss, formerly of Leicester, has been mentioned at Everton also as they anticipate bids for Iliman Ndiaye.

Fulham in for Vallecano defender

Fulham are trying to complete a deal for Rayo Vallecano defender Andrei Ratiu.

The Romania right-back has already approved the move but there had been interest from Nottingham Forest also. The 28-year-old can also play in midfield.

Everton have shown interest in Fulham's Timothy Castagne who has a year left in contract.

Forest in talks over £40m move for Everton teen

Nottingham Forest are continuing attempts to rebuild their midfield following Elliot Anderson’s sale.

They are speaking to Everton about a deal worth £40m for their homegrown 19-year-old midfielder Harrison Armstrong, who started against Crystal Palace last week.

They have enquired about a loan with option to buy Pape Matar Sarr from Tottenham, who also has Monaco interest.

And they are continuing talks with Corinthians for 20-year-old Brazilian Andre.

Forest are close to reaching an agreement with Crystal Palace for Daniel Munoz. Forest made a £22m bid earlier this week and negotiations are at the final stages.

Harrison Armstrong in Everton's opening game of the season against Crystal Palace

Mbaye due to undergo Villa medical

Ibrahim Mbaye is due to undergo his medical later today and complete his transfer to Aston Villa from Paris Saint-Germain over the weekend.

The contract is being finalised and the deal for the 18-year-old is worth £47m.

PSG are making up to £170m from the deals for Bradley Barcola and Mbaye.

Spurs reject loan offer for defender

Tottenham have rejected a loan offer from Sunderland for Kevin Danso.

Sunderland explored the potential of taking the 27-year-old on a season loan.

Tottenham paid £21m for the defender last year

Spurs have rejected a loan offer from Sunderland for centre back Kevin Danso

Barcola set for Liverpool medical

Bradley Barcola is due on Merseyside this weekend to undergo a medical after Liverpool and Paris Saint Germain reached agreement on a £106million fee rising to £123m.

The 23-year-old France international is set sign a Liverpool contract until 2031 after the Anfield club finalised the structure of the transfer over the past 24 hours.

Liverpool are now set to pay £17m in add-ons.

Documents are still to be exchanged between the clubs and details are being arranged for Barcola to travel.

Liverpool are continuing to pursue another winger though Crystal Palace want a substantial fee for Ismaila Sarr after initial conversations last week.

Alternatives are being explored though Sarr, 28, is keen on the move. Palace have also asked about Torino's Alieu Njie and are in the throes of selling Daniel Munoz to Nottingham Forest.

Sports.title: Cody Gakpo wants Man City move: Liverpool star rejects Spurs in favour of Etihad switch with clubs working to strike agreement in deal worth £85MILLION
Sports.content:
Manchester City have opened talks with Liverpool over an audacious bid for Cody Gakpo worth £85million.

The forward, 27, has told Liverpool that if he does leave the club, he wants it to be for Manchester City. Tottenham are also interested.

Liverpool are clear that they want to to sign two more forward players before they contemplate letting go of the Dutchman just three days before the transfer window ends.

They want a substantial fee for a star who is contracted until 2030 after signing a long-term extension last year.

The Reds are set to complete the £123million signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and his preferred position is on the left, where Gakpo often plays.

Gakpo joined Liverpool for £44m in 2023 and has since scored 51 goals in 182 games.

Cody Gakpo has chosen to join Manchester City with the club in talks with Liverpool

He scored in their opening game of the season against Newcastle and assisted Alexander Isak against Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

City are on the hunt for a new wide player after selling Savio to Tottenham for £85m.

But given that fee for a player far less productive than Gakpo, and with Liverpool knowing how much City banked from the deal, the Reds will drive a hard bargain for an important first-team player.

Gakpo was less effective last season but, in their 2024-25 Premier League title-winning campaign, scored 18 goals in all competitions.

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard blasts Liverpool for being 'too nice' - and warns Andoni Iraola must add 'nastiness' to his team or risk being left behind by rivals
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard has blamed Liverpool's slow start to the season on the team being 'too nice'.

And the Reds legend fears that they will miss out on silverware this campaign unless Andoni Iraola can add some 'nastiness' to his squad.

Liverpool were forced to come from behind for a point for the second weekend running as Nottingham Forest earned a 2-2 draw at Anfield on Saturday afternoon.

'I think this Liverpool team is a little bit too nice,' Gerrard told TNT Sports.

They lack a destroyer. They don't make many tackles or win many duels. They're a nice team.

That's the next development for this manager to change this team. They have to be more physical and aggressive.

Steven Gerrard says Liverpool are 'too nice' and need to find more 'nastiness' to win games

It took a moment of brilliance from Victor Munoz to ensure Liverpool took a point at Anfield against Nottingham Forest

'Last week, they would have won that game if they were more up for the duel, up for the tackle, people wanting to take yellow cards, people being nastier, uglier to play against.

'Sometimes you win games a different way. They've got a load of nice technical players, a load of top talents, but they lack nastiness, and that's what the manager has got to get in this team.

'If not, when the big prizes come out at key times of the season, Liverpool won't be there. They lack nastiness and oomph.'

While they dominated the ball with 69 per cent of possession, the champions from two seasons ago managed just four shots on target against Forest.

It took a superb cross from Cody Gakpo to unlock Forest's defence for Alexander Isak's goal, then a sizzling finish from Victor Munoz for the second.

Issues from last season resurfaced: Liverpool were vulnerable to counter-attacks and second-best in physical battles.

They twice had to come from behind. First, Dan Ndoye gave the visitors the lead in the 24th minute after a long ball over the top, then in the second half, Morgan Gibbs-White converted from the penalty spot after Alisson was judged to have fouled Neco Williams.

Iraola was furious at that decision and also how long it took fourth official Tim Robinson to prepare the board for the substitutes, which he was having issues with.

Andoni Iraola would be forgiven for thinking he was watching last season's Liverpool - the same issues keep popping up

They are still vulnerable to counter-attacks, lack ingenuity, and are second-best physically

'With the penalty, the situation has already finished when the contact appears. And it's not an aggressive contact,' Iraola told the BBC.

'But more than this we complained about the subs. We had to wait about three minutes.

'He was having an issue with the board, I don't know if it was not working, but we definitely wanted to do the subs the last two or three stoppages before the goal.

'It wasn't just that reason but everything helps.'

Speaking to TNT Sports, he added: 'A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes. We'd already given him the subs two or three minutes before.

'I was already angry because in the previous stoppage we couldn't make the subs and then before throw-in I thought we could do it.

'I don't know, they will have to explain it. But it has taken ages.'

But Gerrard felt that Liverpool simply should have dealt with the hand they were given better.

'You can understand the frustration - in this day and age, with all the technology, it can't be taking three minutes to make a triple substitution,' he told TNT Sports.

'But I think it's a small problem in the overall problem because it's a goal that can be avoided.'

Sports.title: Spurs fans have seen this all before: £350m worth of new signings are counting for nothing right now as they struggle to banish the problems of last season, writes MATT BARLOW
Sports.content:
Spurs fans have seen this all before: £350m worth of new signings are counting for nothing right now as they struggle to banish the problems of last season, writes MATT BARLOW

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Up went to the board to indicate four minutes of added time and out went the Tottenham fans, heading for the exits and the drizzle of the High Road.

They were damp and deflated, and when the final whistle sounded those who remained summoned what energy they could boo their own team off as Newcastle celebrated victory in N17 for the third season in a row.

They have seen it all before. Too often last season, when Spurs won just three of 19 home games and lost 10.

Roberto De Zerbi wanted nothing to do with that miserable record when asked about it on the eve of this game.

Under him, he pointed out, they had won one and drawn two of three home games.

Nothing to worry about, but the notion Spurs have put all the problems of last season behind them does not ring true yet.

Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa celebrate Wissa's goal that made it 2-0 at Spurs

The summer of unprecedented spending, eight new signings at a cost of more than £350m, and an upbeat message of hope in the programme from chief executive Vinai Venkatesham counted for nothing as they went down to second-half goals by Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa.

Spurs were better than in their opening game against Brentford but not much and two games into the new Premier League season they have no points and no goals.

Here, they made a sluggish start, embodied by captain Micky van de Ven, who did not play in pre-season and came off the bench in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday for his first appearance since the World Cup.

Van de Ven was sleeping as Anthony Elanga eluded him in the opening seconds and gave Newcastle an early chance. Among the reasons for De Zerbi to rush his new skipper back would be to cope with Elanga’s electric pace.

Others in white started slowly, including Sandro Tonali to the delight of the travelling Geordies, who cheered as he was dumped on the turf by a tackle by Joe Willock. Tonali’s poor pass cost Van de Ven short a yellow card.

£100m man Sandro Tonali shakes hands with his boss Roberto de Zerbi after being hooked

Newcastle, who made a positive start to the season against Liverpool after a summer of turmoil, were sharper, dominating the opening 10 minutes with Nico Gonzalez composed on his debut in midfield.

Belatedly, Spurs grew into the game and found some rhythm.

Lukas Hornicek was called into action to make first half saves to deny Mathys Tel cutting in from the left and Jan Paul van Hecke with a header from a corner, and Lewis Hall made a vital block when a miscued shot by Tonali sliced square to Pedro Porro, deployed for the first 68 minutes in a more advanced role than usual on the right wing in the absence of Savio. Porro also lashed a dipping volley over with his left foot in the first half.

Having scored on his Spurs debut in the Carabao Cup against Charlton, £85m winger Savio was ruled out with muscle fatigue, detected on Friday according to De Zerbi, who hopes to have the Brazilian available next week against Nottingham Forest.

There was no Richarlison either in the Spurs squad, amid speculation he may be a makeweight in a move for Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye.

Wissa delivers an acrobatic finish past Antonin Kinsky as Spurs' dreadful start continues

Richarlison is surplus to De Zerbi’s requirements since Omar Marmoush completed his move from Manchester City on Thursday. All of which seemed to outfox Brazil boss Carlo Ancelotti. Ancelotti was in the crowd but there were no Brazilians on the pitch.

Kevin Danso, the subject of a bid from Sunderland to take him on loan, was another not involved.

Marmoush, thrown straight into the team, grew in influence as Spurs came to life midway through the first half, the Egypt international pulling Newcastle’s central defenders out of shape and linking up with the wide players.

His finishing let him down when his first chance dropped to him at the end of the first half. He was lurking deep beyond the back post and unmarked when Andy Robertson’s corner picked him out but Marmoush dragged his effort into the side netting on the volley.

Spurs were on top either side of half-time, but Newcastle resisted and took the lead with an exquisite goal featuring a sweeping pass to the left by Gonzalez and a header down by right back Amar Dedic.

Ecstatic Newcastle fans celebrate a successful trip to the capital

Elanga collected the ball and scored on the turn, an exquisite finish spun inside the far post.

The second also came with aesthetic appeal, this time the craft of a goal poacher able to fashion an effort on goal in the blink of an eye.

Nick Woltemade had been on less than a minute when he won a header at the back post and nodded a corner down into the six-yard box where Wissa finished with an overhead kick.

It was the cue for De Zerbi to haul off Tonali to a burst of ironic cheers from the away fans and send on Dominic Solanke, but there was no way out.

Sports.title: TOTTENHAM 0-2 NEWCASTLE - PLAYER RATINGS: Which new Spurs signing was 'ordinary?' Who marshalled the midfield for the Magpies? And how did Sandro Tonali fare against his old side?
Sports.content:
Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa inflicted a miserable defeat on Tottenham Hotspur with the Newcastle United pair proving prolific in attack.

Spurs started slowly but sprang into life after 20 minutes and played some slick offensive football at times.

But Newcastle hung in there and were clinical in the second half, with two goals in ten minutes imposing Spurs’ second defeat of the season.

Daily Mail Sport's BOBBY MANZI was at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where he rated and slated the stars during an entrhalling contest in North London.

Matthias Jaissle has his first Premier League win as Newcastle boss after beating Spurs 2-0

Tottenham Hotspur (4-2-3-1)

Antonin Kinsky - 6

Not much he could have done about either goal albeit he somewhat flapped at the second. Slightly indecisive when coming off his line.

Archie Gray - 6

Kept Harvey Barnes quiet. Went relatively under the radar.

Jan Paul van Hecke - 6

Was comfortable despite conceding twice. Perhaps a tad slow to react to the corner delivery which gave Newcastle their second. Fine margins.

Micky van de Ven - 5

Relied on van Hecke to bail him out of trouble after he failed to deal with a long ball. Went into the book for a late challenge. Made a superb intervention before the break to prevent Yoane Wissa bombing through on goal. Goal came from his side. Inconsistent.

Micky van de Ven relied on Jan Paul van Hecke to bail him out of trouble

Andy Robertson - 5

Found Omar Marmoush in acres at the far post with a wicked corner delivery. Was too late to track Amar Dedic’s run for the opener.

Rodrigo Bentancur - 5

Wasn’t great in his duels, nor was he particularly imposing. Didn’t do much to get the ball from back to front either.

Sandro Tonali - 5

Picked out plenty of his former teammates as he struggled to find his passing range for the first 15 minutes. Came into it after that, though. Passes were not always perfectly executed but made progressive decisions. Questionable for the opener. Jeered by the away support when withdrawn.

Sandro Tonali was jeered by the Newcastle supporters when he was taken off

Pedro Porro - 6

Made a good fist of playing out of position. Had a wicked volley from outside the penalty area loop just over the bar. Tried to make things happen offensively, particularly in the first half.

Mateus Fernandes - 5

Ordinary in midfield. Did not do much to catch the eye.

Mathys Tel - 6

Forced a big save and worked hard down the left in the first half. Took a woeful free-kick which soared well over the bar. Dropped off after the break.

Omar Marmoush - 6

Not a bad debut, result aside. Showed quick, tricky footwork when on the ball. Threaded some good passes. Dragged a chance wide of the post although the angle was tight. Promising.

Omar Marmoush made an encouraging debut, result aside, and could have scored

Substitutes:

Moore (67, Gray) - 6

Udogie (67, Robertson) - 6

Kudus (67, Tel) - 6

Solanke (74, Tonali) - 6

Manager: Roberto De Zerbi - 6

His forwards were inefficient - he cannot be blamed for that. But his substitutions did not make an impact.

Newcastle United

Lukas Hornicek - 8

Kept Newcastle alive in the first half with two brilliant stops - denying a curling effort from Tel and stopping a van Hecke header from point blank range. Deserves plenty of credit.

Amar Dedic - 7

Looks an intelligent buy at right-back. Played well against Liverpool last weekend. Bright again. His header from the right found Elanga to give Newcastle the lead.

Malick Thiaw - 7

Solid throughout. Gave Newcastle a good platform to build from.

Sven Botman - 7

Saw yellow. Handled the Spurs frontline well.

Lewis Hall - 8

Exceptional performance. Made a huge clearance followed by an even bigger block to deny Spurs the lead. Pinpoint corner delivery as Newcastle added their second.

Nico Gonzalez - 8

Managed 70 minutes and played two crisp balls over the top from deep. Pivotal to Newcastle’s first with a crossfield pass travelling 40 yards. Marshalled midfield well. Will prove an astute addition once fully fit.

Nico Gonzalez marshalled the midfield well and played two crisp balls over the top from deep

Lewis Miley - 7

Consistent. Covered plenty of ground in midfield. Will be tired this evening.

Anthony Elanga - 7

Exquisite finish into the bottom corner with his left foot. Managed to get around Kinsky earlier, too, but could not poke it in.

Joe Willock - 6

Didn’t create bundles as the ten. Fairly absent throughout.

Harvey Barnes - 6

Was kept quiet, with most of Newcastle’s entertaining play coming from the opposite side. Helped keep the solid shape defensively.

Yoane Wissa - 7

Acrobatic finish to wrap up three points for Newcastle. Made some good runs. Not always involved in play but made an impact when he was.

Anthony Elanga scored for the second weekend running as he found the bottom corner

Yoane Wissa looks a man reborn and put in another great performance here, bagging a goal

Subs:

Woltemade (70, Willock) - 7

Steur (70, Gonzalez) - 6

Ramsey (82, Wissa) - N/A

Murphy (82, Elanga) - N/A

Toure (90, Barnes) - N/A

Manager: Matthias Jaissle - 7

His team had to withstand some pressure in the first half but held his nerve. Starting Gonzalez proved a masterstroke.

Referee: Peter Bankes - 6

Was pressured into giving Gonzalez a soft yellow card; otherwise fine.

Sports.title: Newcastle fans revelled in Sandro Tonali's exit after £100m man was hooked... and his replacement Nico Gonzalez looks like twice the player at half the price, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
The cheer when Sandro Tonali’s number was shown 15 minutes from time was just about as loud and hearty as those which had not long greeted Newcastle’s two goals.

‘You should have stayed at a big club’ goaded the Toon Army. The Italian may well wonder what he has stumbled into at Tottenham, and his new employers would be right to wonder when exactly he is going to start looking like a £100million footballer.

His replacement at Newcastle, £50m Nico Gonzalez, looked twice the player at half the price here. It was his cross-field ball that served as the source for Newcastle’s opening goal, scored by Anthony Elanga.

Gonzalez made way a few minutes before Tonali, the Newcastle debutant afforded a rest on the back of a disciplined and diligent performance. When Tonali was then substituted, it was simply because his team needed better.

Sandro Tonali shakes hands with his manager Roberto de Zerbi after being taken off

Nico Gonzalez, signed from Manchester City, outshone Tonali during Newcastle's 2-0 win

In the first 15 minutes, he found more Newcastle shirts than he did towards the end of last season, when it was clear his head was elsewhere. When, though, will it arrive in North London? Of just 36 passes, seven of Tonali’s went astray. Compare that to Gonzalez and 48 of 51 completed.

But Newcastle’s new midfielder was not the only one to impress. Here, we pick through what was a deserved away victory…

ONE EL OF A START

That’s two goals from two matches for Elanga. To think, he did not score at all in the Premier League in his debut season. Last August, he ran through on goal on the opening day against Aston Villa after 30 seconds and fluffed his big chance. It set the tone for a disappointing campaign.

This time, on the back of a good World Cup with Sweden, he is playing like the £55m signing Newcastle were convinced would solve their right-wing problem 12 months ago. Better late than never.

Antonin Kinsky and the Spurs defence could only watch as Anthony Elanga's strike went in

JAISSLE, WE CAN BOOGIE...

They say that dogs can end up reflecting their owners. Well, Jason Tindall may be gone, but in head coach Matthias Jaissle, Newcastle have a new Mad Dog - and his team have the same bark and bite on the pitch.

The German is not one for staying on the leash within his technical zone, but the snarl and energy that sees him take off down the touchline has, so far, inspired his players.

Jaissle is a demonstrative presence and supporters like that, evidenced by them serenading him on full-time with a chorus of, ‘Jaissle, we can boogie’. His Newcastle players are certainly dancing to his tune.

WIS KID YOANE

Yoane Wissa had a nightmare first season on Tyneside. He was injured for the first half and unfit for the second. Now, he is Newcastle’s No.9 and, while not with the armband, he is their on-field leader.

Insiders believe Wissa could be the team’s difference-maker this term, given he scored 19 in the season before last for Brentford. It’s a cliche, but he feels like a new signing.

Yoane Wissa celebrates scoring his side's second goal and insiders believe he could be a difference-maker for Newcastle this season

DED GOOD…

On the subject of signings, right back Amar Dedic has been Newcastle’s best player so far this season, albeit on the back of three matches. But, at £30m, the Bosnian looks a bargain. He is quick, aggressive and has quality on the ball. This was his third assist when teeing up Elanga.

ONE MORE NEEDED…

Newcastle started well. They had territory and possession. They also had no shots on target until their opener in the 62nd minute. There is a reason the club are still active in deals to bring in forwards Matias Fernandez-Pardo, of Lille, and Stuttgart’s Bilal El Khannouss. Sources say both will not be signed, but there is hope that one can be done.

Because over the course of a season, you suspect, Newcastle still do not have enough in attack. They have not replaced the goals of Anthony Gordon, Bruno Guimaraes or, to go back 12 months further, Alexander Isak.

That is the longer-term worry for Jaissle, because his team is executing his instruction when it comes to intensity and front-foot urgency. The manager, then, is pushing for the player he knows they still need, if those foundations are to take his side to the place they deserve.

Sports.title: Dan Lawrence has gone from brink of Test team axe to a man it will be hard to drop as stellar innings in tough conditions moves England towards victory, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
Dan Lawrence began the second Test against Pakistan as the batsman most likely to make way when Jacob Bethell returns for the winter tour of South Africa, but he made impeccable use of a stop-start day at Lord’s to give the selectors pause for thought.

With only 24.5 overs possible between the showers, and conditions as helpful to seam bowling as they can be without the umpires stepping in and declaring a mismatch, Lawrence improvised his way to a half-century to cement England’s grip on both this game and the series.

When play was finally abandoned shortly after 6.30pm in the brightest conditions of the day, his unbeaten 50 had helped turn their overnight 81 for three into 177 for seven, an overall lead of 357. And with better weather forecast on Sunday, that should prove plenty as England go in search of their first series win since December 2024.

Lawrence was into the action soon after the game resumed at 2.20pm. From the day’s 10th delivery, Emilio Gay was pinned leg-before for 31 by a delivery from Mohammad Abbas that did not get above shin height – poor reward for his gutsy batting on Friday evening, and a heart-in-mouth moment for MCC officials who had spent the first two days grateful that none of the chatter had been about the pitch.

It was as bad a moment for the groundstaff as the peashooter from New Zealand’s Matt Henry that scuttled Jacob Bethell here back in June, when the Lord’s pitch was rated ‘unsatisfactory’ by the ICC.

Dan Lawrence hits a slog-sweep six off spinner Ali Usman during a thrilling innings

Mercifully, Gay’s misfortune proved a one-off, but Lawrence decided to take matters into his own hands. His first scoring shot came courtesy of a wild charge at Abbas and a thick edge over the cordon, setting the tone for an innings in which valour was the better part of discretion.

He whipped Khurram Shahzad through the leg side, pulled him for four more, then straight-drove the next delivery for another boundary. But the shot of the innings, and possibly the Test, came off Mohammad Ali. Having carved him over the slips for four, Lawrence went inside-out over extra cover for a majestic six. Later he slog-swept spinner Ali Usman into the Tavern Stand, and was soon bringing up a 64-ball half-century worth perhaps twice as much.

Events at the other end lent his counter-attack further lustre. Harry Brook was superbly caught behind for 34 by Mohammad Rizwan, standing up to Abbas, who then had Jamie Smith caught at square leg for seven.

When Mohammad Ali pinned Gus Atkinson, England were 162 for seven, though with their lead by this stage 342, and Pakistan having totalled 416 runs from three innings so far in this series, the clatter of wickets felt academic.

Mohammad Abbas celebrates the fortunate wicket of Emilio Gay, who can't believe the delivery kept so low

Lawrence’s talent has never been in doubt, though his reputation needed serious repair work after his failed stint as Zak Crawley’s replacement as opener against Sri Lanka two years ago.

‘I was happy to open last time,’ he said. ‘I’d bat anywhere for England, but I wasn’t in the best form. Thankfully I’ve come into this series with some good form behind me, and I’m desperate to establish myself in an England shirt.’

His performance here might have been in homage to Joe Root’s demand for his players to assess conditions and bat accordingly: the risks he took were calculated not brazen, and his sixth Test fifty lit up a grey day.

His fifth, last week in Leeds, left him ‘gutted’ not to have made a bigger score. If he can convert this one into a maiden hundred, the selectors may feel spoiled for choice.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
